summary: 资料照片：这张示意图展示了Meta的标志及一个键盘。(2026年10月19日) 台湾将在下星期六(11月28日)举行九合一地方选举。路透社报道，台湾在选举前夕向社媒巨头Meta举报近2700个疑似与中国有关的社媒账号，怀疑这些账号是中国政府针对台湾“信息战”行动的一部分，以干预和影响台湾下周的选举。 路透社采访了三位不具名的台湾官员后报道说，台湾官员在过去几个星期内发现，这些账号出现在Meta旗下在台湾颇受欢迎的文字类社交平台Threads上，怀疑这些账号被用于协助中国对台湾
content:
资料照片：这张示意图展示了Meta的标志及一个键盘。(2026年10月19日)
台湾将在下星期六(11月28日)举行九合一地方选举。路透社报道，台湾在选举前夕向社媒巨头Meta举报近2700个疑似与中国有关的社媒账号，怀疑这些账号是中国政府针对台湾“信息战”行动的一部分，以干预和影响台湾下周的选举。
路透社采访了三位不具名的台湾官员后报道说，台湾官员在过去几个星期内发现，这些账号出现在Meta旗下在台湾颇受欢迎的文字类社交平台Threads上，怀疑这些账号被用于协助中国对台湾选举的“影响力行动”。
11月28日台湾的“九合一”地方选举将选出9类地方公职人员，包括6个直辖市长、16个县市长，以及县市议员、乡镇市长、里长，应选总名额达11051人。
台湾总统赖清德并不在此次选举的选票上，但是选举却被视为选民对赖清德施政的“期中考”，有些类似于美国刚刚结束的“中期选举”。九合一选举通常也被视为2028年台湾总统大选的一场“前哨战”。
路透社援引台湾政府的一份报告说，这些受到怀疑的账户都是在过去四个月内开设的，而且大多数呈现出批量设置的特征。台湾官员说，其中绝大多数账户来自中国。
中国当局多年来坚称拥有对台湾的主权，而且即使诉诸武力，也要实现两岸的统一，北京常常抨击赖清德政府奉行所谓“台独”分裂的政策。
台湾的民进党政府拒绝北京对台湾的主权诉求，并坚持认为，中华民国早已是一个主权独立的国家，而台湾的未来只能由其2300万人民自行决定。
台湾官员担忧中国政府正加紧在网络上采取行动，试图在选举前影响台湾的选民，以便让北京属意的政党和候选人胜选。
Meta公司发言人在一份声明中向路透社表示，该公司已经删除了台湾政府举报的那些账号，其中许多账号此前就已经被Meta公司自身的系统明令禁用。
Meta还表示，这些都是“低质量虚假账号”，而且也未发布过与选举相关的内容。其中大多数账号都没有关注者。
“我们将继续针对违反我们政策的账号采取行动，”路透社援引该发言人的话说。
路透社曾联络中国国务院台湾事务办公室，寻求对此事的评论，但是没有收到回应。北京长期以来都否认任何有关其干预台湾选举的指控。
三位不具名的台湾官员向路透社表示，中国的这些活动属于其更广泛的虚假信息攻势的一部分。此举旨在放大具有分裂性的政治论述，并试图削弱人们对民主制度的信任。
“他们未必会要求你支持特定的候选人，但会诱导人们相互对立、对民主制度产生反感、选择放弃投票，并加剧选举中的分裂，”路透社援引其中一位官员的话说。
台湾总统府国家安全会议的一名官员向路透社表示，中国利用社媒平台及其他手段，试图影响台湾选举相关的舆论。该官员说，台湾将继续与盟友及负责任的平台合作，确保选举不受外部势力干扰。
台湾官员们表示，由于Threads在台湾广受欢迎，它成为了此次所谓“行动”的目标。但是在Instagram上尚未发现类似的账号。
路透社看到的一份政府报告显示，在台湾标记出的2400个Threads账号中，74%的账号显示其所在地为中国，约25%未注明所在地，另有1%显示为俄罗斯。报告称，这些账号被归为27个群组，它们使用相似的中文名称和不同的数字标识，表明这些账号是批量创建的。
受访的台湾官员表示，这些账号往往先伪装成普通的台湾用户，发布一些关于算命等日常兴趣的内容，以此建立“可信度”。“随后，它们会开始批评政府并攻击候选人，接着声称对执政党感到失望，并因此决定放弃投票，”这名官员说。
路透社报道说，台湾方面还告知Meta公司，约有260个账号传播了超过2150段由超级智能(通常称为人工智能或AI)生成的视频。官员们认为，这些视频也是中国相关行动的一部分。
台湾政府的报告显示，这些视频共获得了235万次互动，包括评论和分享。其中大多数视频针对的是民进党的政治人物及其政策。其中针对民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋的视频指控他在学生时代有过霸凌行为，但沈伯洋本人已否认了相关指控。

# 美民主党议员批特朗普遭习近平普京利用 指美中俄峰会毫无成果

美国总统特朗普（Donald Trump）日前在中国深圳，与中国国家主席习近平及俄罗斯总统普京（Vladimir Putin）举行首次三方峰会，会后虽发表涉及能源供应、联合国改革、国际刑事法院及核扩散等议题的四点“和平宣言”，但未有触及乌克兰及伊朗战争，也未见在核武控制等问题取得具体进展。

发表时间： 20/11/2026 - 22:39

 9 分钟 浏览时间

 2026年11月19日，美国总统特朗普结束中国之行后抵达位于美国华盛顿特区的白宫。 REUTERS - Ken Cedeno

 作者： [华盛顿特约记者 陈米亚](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E9%99%88%E7%B1%B3%E4%BA%9A/ "华盛顿特约记者 陈米亚")

美国民主党两名国会领袖批评特朗普缺乏明确外交策略，参议院外交关系委员会民主党首席议员沙欣（Jeanne Shaheen）更直言，特朗普“毫无疑问”遭习近平及普京利用，整场峰会只是政治宣传，没有为美国带来实际利益。

根据美国MS NOW报道，沙欣接受该台主持人访问时，被问及习近平和普京是否在会谈中“耍了”特朗普，她回答：“毫无疑问。”她指出，三方会谈历时约80分钟，最后没有取得实质成果，形容这只是“一场拍照活动，没有任何具体成果，也没有为美国人民带来任何好处”。

沙欣认为，特朗普此行主要是为了满足个人政治需要，而非维护美国利益。她说，这场会议是为了“让特朗普总统满足自己的自尊心，却没有为美国带来任何成果”。

她也批评特朗普在共和党于期中选举遭遇重大挫败后，仍选择与习近平及普京会面，反映他没有理解美国民众的优先关注事项。沙欣指出，选举结果已反映选民不满特朗普介入伊朗战争，但他却与被指协助伊朗持续战事的两国领袖会面。

她说：“就在两星期前举行的选举中，总统介入伊朗战争，以及发动这场战争的决定，已经遭到选民彻底否定。但他现在却与两个国家的领袖坐下来会谈，而这两个国家正协助伊朗继续这场战争，让伊朗得以攻击中东地区的美国盟友，以及在中东服役的美国军人。”

沙欣同时批评特朗普对普京的态度，指他不断向俄罗斯总统示好，可能削弱美国国家安全。她称普京是“战争罪犯”，指控他涉及将数以千计乌克兰儿童带到俄罗斯，并对他们进行思想灌输，也要为大量乌克兰人及俄罗斯士兵死亡负责。她又指出，俄军每月伤亡人数超过3万人，普京持续对乌克兰发动战争，并试图破坏欧洲及北约（NATO）国家的稳定。

沙欣说：“我无法理解总统为什么如此欣赏普京，还不断与他拉近关系。”她认为特朗普支持普京的做法“会削弱美国的安全”。

另一方面，众议院外交事务委员会民主党首席议员米克斯（Gregory Meeks）也质疑峰会成果。根据美国国家公共电台（NPR）报道，米克斯接受访问时表示，特朗普如果决定与习近平及普京会面，理应事先制定清晰策略及谈判目标。

米克斯说：“我希望他如果打算与这些领袖会面，至少有一套计划和策略，也清楚知道自己想达成什么目标。但显然，他并没有。”

米克斯担心，三国领袖可能讨论重新划分全球势力范围，让美国盟友被排除在重要决策之外，进一步损害美国与盟友的关系。他也批评峰会没有在核武控制及人工智能安全方面取得实质进展。

谈及美中关系，米克斯表示，美方应向习近平直接提出中国涉嫌间谍活动及窃取知识产权的问题，并警告可能采取反制措施。他说：“涉及我们的国家安全时，这就是我们划下红线的地方。”

米克斯认为，美国外交官应在峰会前向中方清楚表明相关关切，建立明确谈判底线。他也主张降低对美国盟友征收的关税，同时要求中国停止支持俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争，以免美国的贸易政策及外交立场削弱盟友合作。

这次三方峰会结束后公布的四点“和平宣言”，涵盖石油生产及供应、联合国改革、国际刑事法院及核扩散，但没有提及乌克兰及伊朗战争。台湾问题也是会谈焦点之一，习近平提醒各方应尊重彼此在敏感议题上的“红线”。

title: The Jet That Always Shadows Air Force One When The President Travels Abroad
zh_title: 当总统出国旅行时，这架喷气式飞机总是尾随空军一号

content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普最近对中国的访问引起了在线航班追踪器的特别关注。这在很大程度上是因为美国空军目前所有三架基于波音 747 的空军一号飞机——两架较旧的 VC-25A 和新的前卡塔尔 VC-25B“桥”喷气式飞机——都支持了这次旅行。另一架军用 747 飞机，即 E-4B 守夜人飞机，通常被称为“世界末日飞机”，也被发现跟踪该组织往返于亚洲。虽然这在网上引起了很多关注，包括来自国防网站的博客文章，但事实是这绝对是标准做法。 E-4B 只是总统离开该国时上演的大型空中物流芭蕾舞剧的另一部分，尽管是一个非常独特和害羞的部分。空军目前拥有四架 E-4B，也称为国家机载作战中心 (NAOC)，全部驻扎在内布拉斯加州的奥法特空军基地。其中三架飞机以 747-200 型号为基础，于 20 世纪 70 年代首次作为 E-4A 高级机载指挥所 (AACP) 投入使用。这些飞机随后在 20 世纪 80 年代达到了 E-4B NAOC 标准，并最终加入了直接改装为该配置的第四架飞机。多年来，这些喷气式飞机不断升级。
除了支持总统旅行外，守夜人飞机还定期在海外旅行期间运送国防部长（现在也称为战争部长）及其工作人员等。E-4B 守夜人喷气式飞机的库存图片。美国军方 11 月 16 日，搭载特朗普及其随行人员的 VC-25 飞机离开华盛顿特区郊外的安德鲁斯空军基地。大约在同一时间，一架 E-4B 被追踪到从奥法特起飞。特朗普首先对菲律宾进行了短暂访问，然后前往中国。飞机观察员有一个难得的机会看到所有三架 VC-25 停在马尼拉尼诺·阿基诺国际机场。美国空军：美国总统随行人员正在经安克雷奇飞往马尼拉的途中。 VC-25B 25-3300 #AF83F3 AF1 VC-25A 92-9000 #ADFDF9 SAM01 VCz25A 82-8000 #ADFDF8 SAM47 @sipjack1776 @toystark6886 @LadyAstroJet pic.twitter.com/jyDtuggNOe — 约翰尼·双子座(@Borrowed7Time) 2026 年 11 月 16 日 守夜人喷气式飞机分别飞往日本冲绳岛的嘉手纳空军基地。 E-4B NAOC 73-1676 在总统马尼拉之行期间停泊在嘉手纳。信用 RODN Kadena。 pic.twitter.com/FiNBpFBsR9 — MeNMyRC (@MeNMyRC1) 2026 年 11 月 17 日 今天早些时候，所有三架 VC-25 载着​​特朗普和美国代表团其他成员离开中国。当三人开始飞越日本本土时，E-4B 从嘉手纳起飞跟随他们。
美国总统返回美国 特朗普总统及其随行人员本周在结束各种会议后正在从中国返回美国的途中： VC-25B Bridge "AF1" 25-33000 #AF83F3 VC-25A "SAM47" 82-8000 #ADFDF8 VC-25A "SAM??" 92-9000 #ADFDF9 E-4B “TRUCK55” 73-1676 #ADFEB3 KC-46A… pic.twitter.com/Yg9wYmgEGI — DefenceGeek (@DefenceGeek) 2026 年 11 月 19 日 正如开头提到的，在特朗普访问期间，E-4B 跟踪 VC-25 并在嘉手纳进行前沿部署先去菲律宾，然后去中国，这并不奇怪。这是美国总统出国旅行的标准操作程序。在特朗普五月份访华期间，飞行追踪器特别发现了类似的飞机队列。 HANK99 又名“末日飞机”(E-4B NAOC) 从内布拉斯加州奥法特空军基地飞往美国

【原文 English Original】
U.S. President Donald Trump’s recent visit to China has drawn particular attention from online flight trackers. This is in no small part due to the fact that all three of the U.S. Air Force’s current Boeing 747-based Air Force One aircraft – the two older VC-25As and the new ex-Qatari VC-25B “Bridge” jet – have supported the trip. Another militarized 747, an E-4B Nightwatch , commonly referred to as a ‘doomsday plane,’ was also spotted shadowing the group to and from Asia. While this drew a lot of attention online, including blog posts from defense-focused sites, the reality is this is absolutely standard practice. The E-4B is just another part, albeit a very unique and shy one, of the massive aerial logistics ballet that occurs whenever the President leaves the country. The Air Force currently has four E-4Bs, also known as National Airborne Operations Centers (NAOC), all based at Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska. Based on the 747-200 model, three of these planes first entered service in the 1970s as E-4A Advanced Airborne Command Posts (AACP). Those aircraft were subsequently brought up to the E-4B NAOC standard in the 1980s, and were eventually joined by a fourth example converted straight to that configuration. The jets have been continuously upgraded over the years. In addition to supporting presidential travel, the Nightwatch aircraft also regularly transport the Secretary of Defense (now also referred to as the Secretary of War) and their staff during overseas trips, among other roles. A stock picture of an E-4B Nightwatch jet. US Military The VC-25s carrying Trump and the rest of his entourage left Andrews Air Force Base just outside Washington, D.C., on November 16. An E-4B was tracked heading out from Offutt at around the same time. Trump headed first for a brief visit to the Philippines before traveling on to China. Plane spotters had a rare opportunity to see all three VC-25s parked together at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila. USAF: POTUS entourage en route to Manila via Anchorage. VC-25B 25-3300 #AF83F3 AF1 VC-25A 92-9000 #ADFDF9 SAM01 VCz25A 82-8000 #ADFDF8 SAM47 @sipjack1776 @toystark6886 @LadyAstroJet pic.twitter.com/jyDtuggNOe — Johnny Gemini (@Borrowed7Time) November 16, 2026 The Nightwatch jet headed separately to Kadena Air Base on the Japanese island of Okinawa. E-4B NAOC 73-1676 bedding down at Kadena during the presidential trip to Manilla. credit RODN Kadena. pic.twitter.com/FiNBpFBsR9 — MeNMyRC (@MeNMyRC1) November 17, 2026 All three VC-25s left China carrying Trump and the rest of the U.S. delegation earlier today. As the trio began to pass over Japan’s home islands, the E-4B took off from Kadena to follow them. POTUS Returning to the US President Trump and his entourage are en-route back to the US from China after various meetings this week: VC-25B Bridge "AF1" 25-33000 #AF83F3 VC-25A "SAM47" 82-8000 #ADFDF8 VC-25A "SAM??" 92-9000 #ADFDF9 E-4B "TRUCK55" 73-1676 #ADFEB3 KC-46A… pic.twitter.com/Yg9wYmgEGI — DefenceGeek (@DefenceGeek) November 19, 2026 As mentioned at the start, the E-4B shadowing the VC-25s and being forward-deployed in Kadena during Trump’s visit to the Philippines and then China is no surprise. This is standard operating procedure for when the President of the United States travels abroad. Flight trackers notably caught a similar procession of aircraft during Trump’s trip to China back in May. HANK99 aka “The Doomsday Plane” (E-4B NAOC) is airborne from Offutt AFB, Nebraska to shadow POTUS on his trip to China. https://t.co/BBsq1tkC1E pic.twitter.com/Z3zpxBX9zy — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) May 12, 2026 While the E-4Bs are nowhere near as luxurious as the VC-25As or the new VC-25B, they are just as capable of serving as airborne command posts, if not more so in many respects . They are unofficially referred to as ‘doomsday planes’ because they are specifically configured to provide the president and other senior military officials with a flying headquarters they can use for any and all duties, including directing nuclear strikes during the most serious crises. They are hardened against electromagnetic pulses caused by nuclear detonations and have the ability to stay airborne for days. Their very existence, at least one being on alert at all times to support the National Command Authority , is a critical component that underpins America’s nuclear deterrent. Even if an adversary destroys much of the country, an E-4 can remain airborne to order the counter-attack. With all this in mind, the E-4B fleet is key to so-called continuity of government plans , which are in place to make sure key elements of the federal government remain functional following an attack or a similarly serious contingency. As a prime example, President George W. Bush rode on one of the VC-25A Air Force One aircraft in the immediate wake of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, but there were discussions about transferring him to a Nightwatch jet . Bush ultimately decided against making the change, but an E-4B was still scrambled and orbited over Washington, D.C., for a time. This is hardly the only time a president has made use of an E-4B, or one of its predecessors, as well as command ships, as TWZ has examined in the past . September 11th, 2001 – Boeing E-4B NAOC callsign ADDIS77 scrambled from Andrews AFB. While ATC was calling them “VENUS” which is a typical callsign used at Andrews, you can hear the urgency of the pilot wanting to get airborne. The E-4 orbited over Washington DC for a while… pic.twitter.com/K61yeFY3kZ — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) September 11, 2021 The aircraft got airborne assuming for safety reasons (safer in air than on the ground) and if needed would have flown to pickup the President or next in the line of succession (Continuity of government). — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) September 11, 2021 Within this broader context, E-4Bs have been a key feature of overseas presidential travel for decades now, although they are the least visible of the presidential aerial armada. This massive airlift and logistics effort includes bringing in multiple examples of the presidential motorcade , Marine One helicopters , and various force protection assets . This involves many sorties by C-17 and C-5 cargo aircraft that cover many thousands of miles each. The videos below from Trump’s visit this week to the Philippines give a sense of just one portion of these options, albeit the most visible one, the vertical airlift component. US President Trump landing at Luneta. Impressive to see the extent of securing the safety of the most important human being on the planet. pic.twitter.com/gIXewN6Yz3 — Emil (@13thFool) November 18, 2026 Beyond its strategic command and control mission, having an E-4B positioned in the region the president is visiting during overseas trips offers a critical option for refuge and escape, as well as an additional backup aircraft to Air Force One, should any emergencies arise. The exact parameters for where the Nightwatch aircraft go are unknown, but would be based on what suitable airports are available and what potential threats and contingencies could arise. They are never seen at the same locations as Air Force One and are always separated by a distance of dozens of miles, at least, in friendly countries — close enough to be accessed by Marine One in an emergency — or generally in a region for more sensitive locales where such close proximity basing isn’t an option. It moves in shadow of AF1 everywhere it goes overseas, usually lands at another airport nearby. This is standard procedure going back decades. We see it every single overseas trip. Beyond it's strategic and COG function it acts as a refuge/escape if something really bad happens… https://t.co/nPhxPJOKMk — Tyler Rogoway (@Aviation_Intel) November 19, 2026 E-4Bs do not need to be airborne to act as command and control platforms and secure communications relay nodes, either. This further feeds into their continuity of government role. These are capabilities that can also be made available, if required, to assist the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) during major natural disasters or to help serve as command posts and communications nodes in other emergencies. The changing character of the Air Force One fleet could put new emphasis on the E-4Bs, as well as the replacement E-4C Survivable Airborne Operations Center (SAOC) jets the Air Force is now in the process of acquiring. Trump’s trip back from China has notably underscored a significant difference between the VC-25As and the new VC-25B Bridge aircraft, which is that the latter lacks aerial refueling capability. Two fully-outfitted VC-25Bs that Boeing is still in the process of converting for the Air Force will also not be capable of refueling in flight. The E-4Bs can refuel in flight, and the E-4Cs will be able to do so, as well. Coming back from China heading to DC, the new VC-25B Bridge Air Force One does not need to refuel in Alaska but the old VC-25As do. Tracking via @ADSBex pic.twitter.com/zhcdCaIRyy — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) November 19, 2026 TWZ has previously explored the Air Force’s decision to axe the aerial refueling requirement for the VC-25B in detail. The ostensible logic is that the VC-25Bs are based on newer 747-8i aircraft with more capable and fuel-efficient engines than the aging 747-200-based VC-25As. The new aircraft are, as a result, capable of longer unrefueled flights, though maximum range requirements were also watered down . At the same time, in-flight refueling allows the VC-25As ( as well as the E-4Bs ) to remain aloft for days at a time. This, in turn, could be critical in a major crisis where access to secure airfields might be limited, if not completely unavailable, for a prolonged period of time. An E-4B links up with a KC-135 aerial refueling tanker. USAF The  VC-25B Bridge jet has prompted a whole new array of operational security questions, which TWZ was calling attention to even before the decision was formally made to outfit it for presidential use. The circumstances of Trump’s return from the NATO summit in Turkey in July had prompted a further flurry of reports about whether the modified, Qatari-gifted jet lacked sufficient defensive features and other capabilities in line with the existing VC-25As. The President had flown to Turkey on the Bridge jet, but was reportedly covertly moved between other aircraft on the way back. This was said to have been done as a security precaution amid then-escalating fighting with Iran . A stock picture of the VC-25B Bridge aircraft seen at the time of its official unveiling. USAF President Trump subsequently downplayed the series of events, but said that the Bridge aircraft would be sent to have its capabilities “maxed out.” The White House confirmed that the jet would receive “additional upgrades and enhancements,” but did not elaborate. It is unclear how the aircraft’s configuration has changed in the ensuing months. It is worth noting here that the upgrades in question would have to be limited to defensive systems. The Bridge aircraft could also have entered service without certain communications and networking capabilities found on the VC-25As. Another way to mitigate any such limitations could be to have a VC-25A or an E-4B operating closely enough to establish a line-of-sight data connection relatively quickly so it can leverage the better-equipped aircraft’s communications systems if needed. As an aside, Trump arrived in China aboard the Bridge aircraft and was seen boarding it to head back to the United States. Reporters onboard had their phones taken away during the return flight for still unexplained security reasons. Fox News has reported that the president is aiming to set a record for the longest continuous flight for an Air Force One aircraft. At the time of writing, its unclear whether the president has touched back down anywhere publicly since leaving Shenzhen. Air Force One is about to take off. Press has had their phones confiscated for security reasons. pic.twitter.com/2UkCDekUma — Andrew Leyden (@PenguinSix) November 19, 2026 NOW: Air Force One is setting a new endurance record on the way home from China. In an exclusive chat with @aishahhasnie , President Trump says his trip back to Washington will be the longest continuous flight in Air Force One history. President Trump says he will discuss the… pic.twitter.com/xn25uSkzYZ — Fox News (@FoxNews) November 19, 2026 Where the E-4B is now is also unclear, but it was last tracked continuing along a path shadowing behind Air Force One, where one would expect to see it. title: Russian Tu-95 Bombers Arrive In Vietnam After Flurry Of Northeast Asia Air Alerts
zh_title: 东北亚空中警报频发后，俄罗斯Tu-95轰炸机抵达越南
summary: 俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动是在中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三方会议前 48 小时举行的。视频屏幕截图显示，Tu-95MS 飞行员于 2026 年 1 月 21 日在日本海上空进行了一次飞行。照片由 Russian Defence Min 摄
content:
俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动是在中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三方会议前 48 小时举行的。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，2026 年 1 月 21 日，一架 Tu-95MS 的飞行员在前一次飞越日本海时。照片由俄罗斯国防部/阿纳多卢通过 Getty Images 拍摄 Anadolu 11 月 16 日至 17 日，Tu-95MS 轰炸机是几架俄罗斯军用飞机之一，在东北亚进行了广泛的演习，引发了三个地区政府的防空反应。据分析师 AviVector 称，共有五架涡轮螺旋桨动力轰炸机于 11 月 16 日从俄罗斯远东的乌克兰基地起飞。据报道，其中三架轰炸机在三架 Il-78M Midas 空中加油机的支援下，在日本海上空进行了大约 11 小时的训练飞行。据报道，一架 A-50U Mainstay 空中预警和控制飞机也在日本海上空飞行。与此同时，另外两架 Tu-95MS 继续向南驶向越南。今天，乌克兰空军基地的三架 Tu-95MS 和三架 Il-78M 在日本海上空进行了 11 小时的训练飞行。
一架 A-50U（RF-94268，红色 41）从符拉迪沃斯托克机场起飞，在日本海上空进行了一次侦察飞行。两架 Tu-95MS（RF-94202，红色 43；RF-94188，红色 44）… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) 11 月 17 日， 2026 日本和台湾均未正式确定参与各自空域事件的飞机类型。日本防卫省证实，11 月 17 日早些时候，两架据信是俄罗斯的飞机侵犯了福冈县冲之岛西北部的领空。第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分左右进入，于凌晨 4 点 10 分起飞。第二架飞机于凌晨 4 点 09 分左右进入，于 2026 年 4 月 10 日起飞。据日本防卫省称，凌晨 4 点 12 分，日本认为俄罗斯飞机于 11 月 17 日早些时候进入福冈附近冲之岛西北部的日本领空，第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分左右进入，第二架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分左右进入日本领空。 pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — 台湾安全监察站 (@TaiwanMonitor) 2026 年 11 月 17 日，日本防卫省称，日本航空自卫队 (JASDF) 派出西方防空部队的战斗机发出警告并采取其他措施。
穿过对马海峡后，飞机在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后继续进入太平洋。 2026年11月17日，推测的俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本联合参谋部 该航线使飞机经过连接日本海、东海和西太平洋的几个具有重要战略意义的海上通道。据报道，俄罗斯飞机随后进入韩国防空识别区（KADIZ）。不过，据韩国国防部称，此次事件并未侵犯韩国领空。

【原文 English Original】
Russia has sent a pair of Tu-95MS Bear bombers for a rare visit to Vietnam. Unusually, the aircraft appear to have briefly intruded into Japanese airspace and passed through Taiwan’s Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ) along the way. The activity unfolded just 48 hours before Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S. President Donald Trump are due to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China. A screen grab from a video shows the pilot of a Tu-95MS during a previous flight over the Sea of Japan on January 21, 2026. Photo by Russian Defense Ministry/Anadolu via Getty Images Anadolu The Tu-95MS bombers were among several Russian military aircraft conducting extensive maneuvers across Northeast Asia on November 16-17, prompting air defense responses from three regional governments. According to analyst AviVector , a total of five of the turboprop-powered bombers departed their home base of Ukrainka in Russia’s Far East on November 16. Three of the bombers reportedly conducted an approximately 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan, supported by three Il-78M Midas aerial refueling tankers. An A-50U Mainstay airborne early warning and control aircraft was also reported operating over the Sea of Japan. Meanwhile, the other two Tu-95MS continued south towards Vietnam. Today, three Tu-95MS and three Il-78M from Ukrainka Air Base conducted an 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan. An A-50U (RF-94268, 41 Red) from Vladivostok Airport conducted a reconnaissance flight over the Sea of Japan. Two Tu-95MS (RF-94202, 43 Red; RF-94188, 44… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) November 17, 2026 Neither Japan nor Taiwan officially identified the aircraft types involved in their respective airspace incidents. Japan’s Ministry of Defense confirmed that two separate aircraft believed to be Russian violated its territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, in Fukuoka Prefecture, early on November 17. The first aircraft entered at approximately 4:07 a.m. local time and departed at 4:10 a.m. A second aircraft entered at approximately 4:09 a.m. and departed at 4:12 a.m. Two aircraft Japan believes are Russian entered Japanese territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, off Fukuoka, early Nov. 17, per Japan's Ministry of Defense. The first was inside from about 4:07 to 4:10 a.m. local time and the second from about 4:09 to 4:12 a.m. The Japan… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — Taiwan Security Monitor (台灣安全觀測站) (@TaiwanMonitor) November 17, 2026 The Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) scrambled fighters from its Western Air Defense Force to issue warnings and take other measures, according to the country’s Ministry of Defense. Tokyo subsequently lodged what it described as a strong protest with Moscow over the incident. Japan also provided details of the aircraft’s subsequent route. After passing through the Tsushima Strait , the planes flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan before continuing into the Pacific Ocean. Flight path of the presumed Russian aircraft on November 17, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office The route placed the aircraft through several strategically important maritime approaches connecting the Sea of Japan , East China Sea , and western Pacific. The Russian aircraft then reportedly entered South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ). However, there was no violation of South Korean airspace, according to the South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff. Finally, Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense reported detecting two Russian military aircraft entering its ADIZ from the northeast. Overall, 2 sorties of Russian military aircraft were detected early this morning. The aircraft entered #Taiwan 's ADIZ from the northeast, flew through airspace east of Taiwan, and exited the ADIZ south of Taitung. The #ROCArmedForces have monitored the situation and responded… — 國防部 Ministry of National Defense, ROC(Taiwan) (@MoNDefense) November 17, 2026 The aircraft proceeded through airspace east of Taiwan before exiting south of Taitung. Taiwan’s armed forces monitored the activity and responded accordingly, the Ministry of National Defense said. The incident is notable because Taiwan’s defence ministry publicly identified the aircraft as Russian, rather than simply reporting unidentified military aircraft activity. As we have reported in the past , Chinese aircraft commonly fly into the southwestern part of Taiwan’s ADIZ. It is, however, worth noting that the ADIZ declared by Taiwan covers not only the entirety of the Strait but also portions of mainland China. In terms of Russian aircraft operating in Taiwan’s ADIZ, there are historical precedents, but such activity has been greatly reduced since the end of the Cold War. Taiwanese military analyst Chieh Chung told Focus Taiwan that Soviet and Russian military aircraft had previously operated inside Taiwan’s ADIZ in 1986 and January 2010. "The incident was not the first time Russian or former Soviet military aircraft had entered Taiwan's ADIZ, although such flights have become much less frequent since the end of the Cold War." https://t.co/TPUJL9hfp1 https://t.co/SDB6p3E3pD — Bryce C. Barros 白若詩 (@barros_bryce) November 17, 2026 The two remaining Tu-95MS aircraft continued south towards Vietnam and were subsequently reported at Da Nang on November 17. They were accompanied by a pair of Il-76MD Candid transports, one of which was a modernized -90A variant , to support the deployment. Tu-95MS strategic missile carriers RF-94202, RF-94188. Il-76MD, Da Nang Airport / "Danang 35K Feet". pic.twitter.com/22DaoD8PLP — Massimo Frantarelli (@MrFrantarelli) November 17, 2026 [Russie Vietnam] 2 Tu-95MS des forces aérospatiales russes sont arrivés à l'aéroport international de Da Nang (DAD/VVDN), au Vietnam. 2 avions de transport militaire IL-76 (MD et MD-90A) les accompagnaient. (c) AviaNews pic.twitter.com/4bWfFXFOik — La souris (@La_souris_DA) November 17, 2026 The flights took place against the backdrop of preparations for the November 19 meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin in China. The summit is set to be held on the sidelines of meetings of the  Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), which kick off tomorrow. Putin arrived in Shenzhen today. Trump has traveled first to the Philippines as part of a short tour of Asia before heading to China. Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen in the early hours of Nov. 18 to attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. ： @PDChina pic.twitter.com/5YotpjYY6R — Shenzhen Daily (@szdaily1) November 17, 2026 The proximity of the Russian operation to the Shenzhen meeting raises questions about the strategic signaling of the Russian flights, particularly as the three governments prepare to discuss nuclear arms control, regional security, and other major international issues. The meeting is particularly unusual given the different priorities each leader is bringing to the table . Trump has indicated that he wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals and addressing the war in Iran. The expiration of the New START treaty in February 2026 removed the remaining bilateral limits on U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear forces, adding urgency to the question of future arms-control arrangements. U.S. President Barack Obama, at left, and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, at right, shake hands after signing the New START treaty in 2010. Government of Russia Washington has tempered expectations of an immediate agreement, describing the gathering as an initial opportunity for the three nuclear powers to begin a conversation. Putin, meanwhile, is expected to seek discussion of Russia’s war against Ukraine and the possibility of a negotiated settlement. Moscow has signalled that Ukraine will remain a priority in its discussions with Washington. Beijing’s position is more cautious. China has resisted joining trilateral nuclear arms-control negotiations at this stage, arguing that its nuclear arsenal remains substantially smaller than those of the United States and Russia. Xi is also seeking to present China as a central diplomatic actor capable of facilitating dialogue between the other two powers. An apparent new field of Chinese intercontinental ballistic missile silos identified by Matt Korda and Hans Kristensen from the Federation of American Scientists (FAS) and located near the city of Hami in the eastern end of Xinjiang province, in the northwest of China. Kristensen/Korda/FAS 2021 The timing of the Russian aviation activity is therefore difficult to ignore. The operation demonstrated the geographic reach of Russian long-range aviation, with aircraft moving from Russia’s Far East through the approaches to Japan and Taiwan before continuing towards Vietnam. The Southeast Asian nation was a regular late Cold War operating location for Soviet naval Tu-95 Bear reconnaissance aircraft. Of course, as well as strategic signalling, flights of this kind provide valuable long-range training and intelligence collection, including assessment of regional air defense responses. The November 19 meeting may not produce an agreement on nuclear weapons or other major disputes. Still, the Russian flights underscore the fact that strategic stability in the Indo-Pacific also involves the security concerns of the regional states operating along the approaches to the western Pacific. content:
唐纳德·特朗普总统在白宫简报室举行的新闻发布会上讲话，副总统万斯和国务卿卢比奥站在他的身后聆听。(026年11月20日)
唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统星期五(11月20日)在白宫表示，美国正与中国商谈一项“非常全面的协议”(very comprehensive deal)。在结束亚洲之行、返回华盛顿后的记者会上，有记者问他，与中国国家主席习近平在深圳会晤后，他是否考虑放宽对华芯片出口限制。特朗普说，他主张只向中国出售更旧版的芯片，即便一块也不卖，他也不介意。
“我们希望只卖更旧版的芯片，一块都不卖也没关系。但要卖就只卖更旧版的，”特朗普说。他接着解释说：“要知道，中国也生产芯片。如果我们不卖给他们，他们就会自己造。”特朗普没有说明他所说的全面协议会包括哪些内容。
星期四的深圳会晤是特朗普与习近平继北京和华盛顿两次会晤后，今年第三次面对面会谈。特朗普星期五特别提到，习近平亲自到深圳机场迎接他。
美国智库史汀生中心中国项目高级研究员孔明尚(Michael Cunningham)在给美国之音(VOA)的书面答复中说，两位领导人保持接触有助于稳定关系，但这次会谈取得的实质成果有限，部分原因是双方在各自最看重的问题上分歧仍大。
孔明尚说：“双方就对方贸易休战的落实情况都不满意。”
对英伟达(Nvidia)和超威半导体(AMD)等美国芯片制造商来说，特朗普的表态留下了一个直接关系到订单的问题：究竟哪些芯片可以卖？
风险咨询公司化险集团(Control Risks)政治与监管风险分析师丹尼尔·雷克沙芬(Daniel Rechtschaffen)在接受美国之音采访时说，特朗普没有给出区分新旧芯片的技术标准。芯片更新换代很快，企业要看美国商务部工业与安全局(BIS)如何界定“更旧版”，以及该局在审批出口许可证时会采取多严格的尺度。
“特朗普的言论可能让一些人看到有限销售的希望，但目前还很难以此为可靠依据，决定是否投资、是否进入这个市场，”雷克沙芬说。
就在特朗普出访前，美国商务部星期一公布新规，收紧对先进“超级智能”(通常被称为人工智能或AI)芯片和服务器的管制。新规针对的是远程使用算力：即使芯片本身没有运入中国，中国企业仍可能通过设在第三国的数据中心，使用美国芯片训练人工智能模型。
特朗普星期五还警告说，对于试图在海外建设数据中心的企业，美国将予以重罚。他表示担心中国会利用这些设施，并点名提到芬兰的一个拟建项目。他说：“他们想在芬兰建那个数据中心，我们不会允许。”
研究美国技术和出口管制政策的克里斯·麦奎尔(Chris McGuire)在社交平台X上写道，特朗普的表态显示，政府既担心中国使用美国芯片和数据中心，也担心数据中心和人工智能产业本身外移。如果美国把这些产业留在国内定为政策目标，那将是“人工智能基础设施政策的一次重大转变”。
麦奎尔认为，本周针对芯片走私和远程使用算力的新管制是有益的第一步，但仍有缺口。他说，目前多数企业在海外建设大型数据中心仍无须事先取得美国政府批准，也没有必须在美国建设的要求。他主张改变这一做法。
雷克沙芬说，中国目前仍相当依赖海外算力，但无论华盛顿是否允许美国企业扩大对华销售，北京都会继续推动芯片国产化。孔明尚则指出，美国国会仍有不少议员主张对华采取更强硬的立场。他预计，美国出口管制可能进一步收紧，美中之间的技术竞争也会加剧。
台湾在星期五的白宫记者会上并未成为主要议题，但中国外交部在前一天发布的美中元首会晤通稿中专门提到台湾。据中方通稿，习近平敦促美方“要坚持做正确的事”，以免两国关系遭遇挫折。中方通稿还说，特朗普向习近平表示，美国不支持“台独”。
“如果北京的说法准确，那么特朗普只是重申了美国长期以来不支持台湾独立的政策，”孔明尚对美国之音说。他认为，特朗普今年三度与习近平会晤后，美国在台湾问题上的公开表述没有出现明显变化，这可能让台北官员松了一口气。
雷克沙芬说，从习近平这次谈及台湾的措辞来看，他没有看到比以往会晤更令人担忧的信号。化险集团评估，未来一两年台海爆发战争的可能性仍然很低。他更关注的是尚未达到战争程度、却可能影响台湾民众和企业的风险，包括网络攻击、海底电缆受损，以及北京对台湾施加贸易压力。
特朗普总统也谈到他在深圳与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladimir Putin)的会晤。星期四，特朗普先后与普京和习近平分别会面，随后三人举行会谈。特朗普星期五在白宫的记者会上说，他认为达成结束俄罗斯对乌克兰战争的协议“很有希望”。被问及美国会向乌克兰提供何种安全保障时，他表示，希望等达成协议后再谈。
美中俄三国领导人在会后发表的共同宣言中同意，就降低核风险和防止核武器扩散展开对话。不过，三方没有公布启动核军控谈判的时间表。特朗普星期五说，他认为，中国的核武库可能在十年内赶上美国。
雷克沙芬认为，普京可能是这场三方会谈最大的受益者：他无须在乌克兰问题上作出让步，就获得了在国际舞台上与美中领导人并肩亮相的机会。习近平则借东道主身份展示了中国的外交影响力。对华盛顿而言，雷克沙芬说，去年双方相继加征关税、收紧出口管制，今年两国元首能保持直接沟通，本身就有助于稳定关系。

Research agency and consultancy Polaris Market Research predicts that the rare earth permanent magnet market will grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.7% between 2026 and 2034 to reach a value of $39.23-billion, compared with $21.81-billion in 2025.
Rising demand from electric vehicles (EVs), industrial automation, wind energy and defence applications is supporting growth in this market, while manufacturers work to reduce their dependence on China, developing alternative sources of supply.
Non-China rare earth permanent magnet supply is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.8% while heavy rare earth-free and reduced-grade magnets are expected to grow by 9.22% between 2026 and 2034.
Earlier this month, China's Ministry of Commerce extended the suspension of its expanded rare earth export controls to January 10, 2027. The pause covers licensing requirements for additional medium and heavy rare earths, rare earth processing equipment and technology, and certain foreign-made products containing 0.1% or more Chinese-origin rare earth content.
However, licensing requirements for seven medium and heavy rare earth elements, including dysprosium and terbium, that were introduced in April 2025 remain in place.
The extension buys manufacturers more time, but it does not eliminate rare earth supply chain concerns.
Polaris reports China's rare earth magnet exports reached 6 165 t in September, the highest this year, as overseas buyers built inventories ahead of the January deadline.
"Companies that use rare earth magnets are increasingly qualifying alternative suppliers and investing in production capacity outside China," the consultancy states.
Polaris says replacing existing rare earth permanent magnet supply is difficult given the scale of China's production capacity and supplier network. Additionally, new facilities need time to reach consistent output and quality and limited mining, separation and refining capacity outside of China also restricts access to raw materials.
Commenting on China's suspension of expanded rare earth export controls to January next year, Polaris senior analyst Apurva Agarwal says the January deadline is a temporary relief, not a permanent solution. "Magnet buyers have realised that export rules can quickly change, making it more important to develop alternative suppliers. In coming years, manufacturers outside China will have more opportunities if they can match the quality and production capacity of established suppliers."
By magnet type, neodymium-iron-boron magnets dominated the market with a 66% share in 2025. Their high magnetic strength makes them ideal for EV motors, industrial systems and consumer electronics, while samarium-cobalt magnets are projected to grow at a CAGR of 6.39% because they perform well under high temperatures and demanding conditions, particularly in aerospace and defence.
By manufacturing process, sintered magnets held the largest share of 70.14% in 2025, as they are widely used in high-performance electric motors and industrial equipment. Bonded magnets are projected to grow at the fastest CAGR of 7.13% owing to their flexible shapes and easy integration into different products.
By heavy rare earth content, standard grades accounted for 72.6% of the market in 2025. Heavy rare earth-free and reduced-grade magnets are projected to grow at a CAGR of 9.22% as manufacturers cut their use of dysprosium and terbium and lower their dependence on restricted materials.
By end use, the automotive segment led with a 39.52% share in 2025, as EV drive systems support growth in the permanent magnet motor market. Wind and renewable energy is projected to grow at the fastest CAGR of 7.61% as countries expand renewable power generation.
By supply chain origin, China-linked supply made up 81.6% of the market in 2025. Non-China supply is projected to grow at the fastest CAGR of 10.85% as manufacturers seek more sourcing options and stronger supply chains.
Asia Pacific dominated the market with a 46.63% share in 2025, reflecting China's established rare earth processing and magnet manufacturing base. Blog War Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

19日に中国・深圳（しんせん）で開催された米中露3カ国の首脳による会談は「新ヤルタ会談」とも呼ばれた。第二次世界大戦末期の1945年2月、ルーズベルト米大統領、チャーチル英首相、スターリン・ソ連（現ロシア）首相が、戦後の国際秩序を決めた「ヤルタ会談」になぞらえたのである。
今回の「新ヤルタ会談」でも特に中国が、米中露は第二次大戦の戦勝国であるとの立場を強調した。中国にとって、この枠組みは日本を牽制するうえで好都合に違いない。その証左ともいえる動きが10月、米ニューヨークの国連本部であった。
中国政府が、極東国際軍事裁判（東京裁判）の開廷80年を記念する写真展を開催したのである。「全人類のための正義と平和」と題し、東京裁判の法廷内の写真や「A級戦犯」に対する判決一覧表などを展示した。
中国の国連大使は開幕式で「日本は東京裁判から一歩一歩背きつつあり、平和国家から徐々に離れていっている」などと訴えた。日本政府は東京裁判を受け入れ、戦後の歩みを進めた。事実を無視したプロパガンダの一環といえるだろう。
一方で、東京裁判を巡っては歴史認識や裁判そのもののあり方について、さまざまな議論がある。特に学校教育においては、過度に自国を卑下する、いわゆる「東京裁判史観」への懸念は根強い。歴史教科書の記述は重要だ。

content:
资料照片：美国芯片巨头英伟达(Nvidia)标识。(2026年6月11日)
美国众议院外交事务委员会星期四(11月19日)发布声明指出，截至今年5月，美国商务部已批准向中国出售87.9万枚超级智能(通常称人工智能或AI)芯片，其中包含阿里巴巴、腾讯等中国科技企业。
众议院外交事务委员会星期四在声明中指出，委员会主席，来自佛罗里达州的共和党联邦众议员布莱恩·马斯特(Brian J. Mast)行使了《出口管制改革法案》所赋予的职权，公开披露有关英伟达(NVIDIA)和超威半导体(AMD)向中国出口人工智能芯片的许可申请信息。
披露内容显示，从2025年12月至2026年5月期间，美国企业共申请向中国出售340万枚人工智能芯片，其中超过87.9万枚获得了美国商务部工业和安全局(BIS)的批准。
其中，阿里巴巴获得7.5万枚、腾讯15万枚、百度4.3万枚、比亚迪4000枚，这些中国企业都在美国五角大楼的具有中国军方背景企业的名单上。相关信息意味着工业和安全局在特朗普政府2025年12月重新开放英伟达先进H200芯片对华销售后，放行了规模庞大的芯片流量。
此外，披露信息还显示，英伟达曾寻求利用可能充当芯片走私掩护的渠道，来促成其向中国企业销售先进人工智能芯片。声明表示，这是《出口管制改革法案》实施以来，最详尽的一次公开披露。
针对芯片出售对象包含中国军事相关企业，美国之音向五角大楼发出置评请求，五角大楼回应让记者询问美国商务部。美国商务部和白宫至报道发表前，未做出回复。
本月稍早，英伟达前CEO黄仁勋因卷入婚外情和中国间谍疑云而辞去职务。
众议院外交事务委员会主席马斯特、众议院中国问题特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)以及众议院常设情报特别委员会主席里克·克劳福德(Rick Crawford)要求黄仁勋以及英伟达到国会作证，以了解英伟达出售先进芯片给中国的有关情况。
星期二(11月17日)三位委员会主席宣布，黄仁勋和英伟达法律顾问蒂姆·泰特(Tim Teter)已经同意出席12月初委员会举行的闭门会议。
三位主席表示，期待听取黄仁勋和泰特的说明：“美国民众需要得到答案：黄仁勋及英伟达在允许危险的中国行为体获取美国最先进芯片的过程中究竟扮演了什么角色？此外，在这起丑闻中，是否有潜在的中国情报人员参与其中？”
同一天，英伟达也宣布，已经停止向中国出售先进的H200芯片。
在黄仁勋辞职后接任临时首席执行官的英伟达首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress) 在财报电话会议上证实，公司已停止向中国出货H200超级智能芯片。
克雷斯表示，英伟达在截至10月25日的第三季度内，向中国出售了价值24亿美元的Hopper数据中心产品，但第四季度展望已将相关营收归零。

Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Nurnisa Kurban is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Uyghur Academic Foundation.
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

content:
Fundraiser by Aydin Anwar : Uyghur Students in Egypt
Aydin Anwar is organizing this fundraiser.
Help save Muslim Uyghur students in Egypt from deportation to China, where they will face detention, persecution, torture, lengthy prison sentences, and perhaps even death.
Hundreds of Muslim Uyghur students in Egypt with resident permits are currently being rounded up to be deported to China, where they will be subject to persecution, imprisonment, torture, and death sentences. Their crime? Being Uyghur and studying Islam. #SaveUyghurStudents
In its attempt to "crackdown on Islamic extremism", China has significantly tightened its security measures and prohibition of religious practice in East Turkestan (aka Xinjiang, occupied by China). Chinese authorities are now seeking the return of thousands of innocent Uyghur students abroad in "wide sweeps" to extend this crackdown.
It has been reported that all airports in Egypts are preventing Uyghurs from leaving the country. Some Uyghur students have already been deported, and the remaining are either in detention awaiting deportation or in hiding within Egypt’s borders. Several that we know managed to escape to Turkey, but are currently homeless or in extreme financial hardship.
Therefore the funds we collect will go to providing shelter, food and other support to the Uyghurs who have already managed to flee Egypt. It will also go to provide those in hiding with necessities (e.g. food, room, board) while we work with nonprofit human rights organizations to pressure Egypt and China to stop the deportations and detentions.
The funds will be collected through Uyghur Youth Campaign, a 501(c) nonprofit based in the US, and will (for now) be directly delivered to the Uyghur students who fled to Turkey by one of its members, Aydin Anwar, who has been in Istanbul. She is connected with these refugees through Munevver Ozuygur, an Uyghur activist based in Zeytinburnu, Istanbul.
Please donate and help spread awareness. Do not remain silent as these young men and women are sent off to be detained, tortured, imprisoned and perhaps even killed in China. They need our help.

title: Community-Focused Academic Brings AI Tools to Colorado Farmers
zh_title: 以社区为中心的学术界为科罗拉多州农民带来人工智能工具
summary: 科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”东 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县扩建项目 Tit
content:
科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”董 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县推广 职称 推广区域专家 会员等级 高级会员 母校内蒙古师范大学，位于呼和浩特；北京师范大学；纽约州立大学环境科学与林业学院，位于锡拉丘兹；科罗拉多州立大学全球分校 她构建了人工智能驱动的农业旅游聊天机器人 (AgriTourismAI.com)，帮助农民和牧场主启动和经营“农业旅游”业务。农业旅游是指农民向游客开放他们的土地以进行娱乐、教育或购物活动。常见的例子包括采摘自己的果园、如何种植蔬菜的课程以及手工产品的销售。董还举办研讨会，向农民和牧场主展示如何使用人工智能工具来帮助发展和管理他们的业务。她说她将自己视为大学和农村之间的纽带。 “我们（推广专家）充当桥梁，”她说。
“我们将校园与我们服务的农村社区联系起来。”许多农民和牧场主年龄较大，通常没有接受过技术培训。他们的子孙常常离开农场到城市工作，或者无法教他们新工具。如果没有帮助，人工智能的好处可能会与农民失之交臂。 Dong 的研讨会为他们提供了一条出路。Dong 凭借她的 AgriPivot AI Agent 入围 2026 年 GenAI for Good Challenge 决赛。该挑战赛由 IEEE Humanarian Technologies 和联合国国际电信联盟组织，她的项目是从 79 个国家的 318 个团队中选出的。她还获得了国家推广技术社区 (NETC) 颁发的 2026 年创新奖，以及国家社区发展推广专业人员协会 (NACDEP) 颁发的 2025 年国家和西部地区教育技术奖。作为首席研究员或联合首席研究员，她获得了七项竞争性资助，总额超过 25 万美元，其中包括由农业部国家食品和农业研究所支持的资金。董出生于北京，从小就热爱设计和解决问题。她的父母都是医生。小时候，她喜欢画新的、有创意的东西。她说，素描可以让她用图片解决脑海中的问题，并将它们作为实际设计写在纸上。这个习惯逐渐成为她与周围环境相处的一种方式。
她说：“我一直热衷于创造一些有形的东西来解决现实世界中的问题。”她并不将自己的人生方向归功于任何一位导师。相反，她说她所有的老师都帮助她为她的职业生涯奠定了基础。她就读于位于呼和浩特的内蒙古师范大学，这是一所培训教师的机构。 2013 年，她在那里获得了两个学士学位——一个是地理科学学士学位，另一个是教育学士学位。然后，她获得了课程和教学硕士学位

【原文 English Original】
Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water. She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain , helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park. In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County ’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns. She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds. Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System , a nationwide network run by land-grant universities , schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states. The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture , managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties. The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program , which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship. Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person. She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says. “We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says. Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI . The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly. How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree , in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global . She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python , a popular programming language . It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT ’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it. The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download. Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk. One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch , in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases . Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication. Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) . The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing. She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude , and Gemini . She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp ., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp ., Colorado Startup Week , and Boulder Startup Week . And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel. Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools , she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use. She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says. Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.” How IEEE membership supports her career Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology . She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group . IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences. IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.” She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE. Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone. “They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

title: The United States’ Participation in the 2026 East Asia Summit
zh_title: 美国参加2026年东亚峰会
summary: 发言人办公室 美国参加2026年东亚峰会情况介绍 2026年11月18日 在11月17日于菲律宾马尼拉举行的东亚峰会上，美国重申对自由开放印太的承诺，表示支持东盟中心地位，并强调美国是该地区首选的能源和技术伙伴。为在美国与东盟建立关系50周年之前推进全面战略伙伴关系，美国和东盟通过了《落实美国-东盟领导人共识的全面工作计划》
content:
发言人办公室 美国参加2026年东亚峰会情况介绍 2026年11月18日 在11月17日于菲律宾马尼拉举行的东亚峰会上，美国重申对自由开放印太的承诺，表示支持东盟中心地位，并强调美国是该地区首选的能源和技术伙伴。为了在美国-东盟关系成立50周年之前推进全面战略伙伴关系，美国和东盟通过了《实施美国-东盟领导人共同愿景声明的综合工作计划，以促进东盟和美国更强大、更安全和更繁荣》（2026-2030年）。美国强调其与盟友和伙伴一道致力于加强威慑，以维护印太地区的和平与稳定。在两国建交80周年之际，美国祝贺菲律宾成功担任东盟轮值主席国。促进和平，加强自由开放的印太地区 美国将继续在印太地区发挥领导作用，并威慑该地区任何试图通过武力解决争端的国家，这体现了特朗普总统通过实力实现和平的承诺。
美国将继续维护《联合国海洋法公约》所反映的国际法规定的所有国家行使航行和飞越自由的权利，包括在南中国海。台海的和平与稳定对于印太地区的安全与繁荣仍然至关重要，美国反对任何单方面改变现状的行为。美国仍然致力于实现朝鲜完全无核化，并全面执行联合国安理会所有涉朝决议。扩大贸易、能源和技术联系美国仍然是东盟最大的单一国家外国直接投资者，截至 2025 年，该地区的外国直接投资超过 5,570 亿美元，为美国提供了约 532,000 个就业岗位。美国祝贺东盟领导人签署《数字经济框架协议》，该协议有可能为美国科技公司提供更大的机会，让该地区的数字经济到2030年将达到2万亿美元。随着美国超级智能（SI）技术在全球树立黄金标准，美国正在与东南亚伙伴合作，扩大获得美国技术的机会，包括通过美国-东盟SI SPARK计划，这将有助于释放该地区的经济潜力。
通过签署《人工智能机会声明》，越南和柬埔寨与其他国家一道致力于促进基于可信赖伙伴关系的创新。为了支持该地区的人工智能准备工作，美国将与印度尼西亚政府、东盟秘书处和卡内基梅隆大学合作，于 12 月在雅加达举办东盟人工智能周。美国和菲律宾签署了一项为期五年的经济繁荣和韧性战略目标协议，该协议将动员对包括吕宋经济走廊在内的关键基础设施的投资，并与可靠的合作伙伴一起确保供应链的安全。作为世界上最大的能源生产国之一，美国可以为东南亚几代人的增长提供动力。美国准备与东盟合作加强该地区的能源安全

Office of the Spokesman The United States’ Participation in the 2026 East Asia Summit Fact Sheet November 18, 2026 At the East Asia Summit in Manila, Philippines on November 17, the United States reaffirmed its commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific, expressed support for ASEAN centrality, and underscored the United States as the region’s preferred partner for energy and technology. To advance their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership ahead of the 50 th anniversary of U.S.-ASEAN relations, the United States and ASEAN adopted the Comprehensive Work Plan to Implement the U.S.-ASEAN Leaders’ Joint Vision Statement to Promote a Stronger, Safer, and More Prosperous ASEAN and America (2026-2030). The United States highlighted its commitment, with allies and partners, to strengthen deterrence to safeguard peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region. The United States congratulated the Philippines on a successful ASEAN chair year, as the two countries mark 80 years of diplomatic relations. Promoting Peace and Strengthening a Free and Open Indo-Pacific Reflecting President Trump’s commitment to peace through strength, the United States will continue to lead in the Indo-Pacific and deter any nation in the region tempted to settle disputes by force. The United States will continue to uphold the right of all nations under international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Seas (UNCLOS) to exercise freedom of navigation and overflight, including in the South China Sea. Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait remain essential to the security and prosperity of the Indo-Pacific and the United States opposes any unilateral change to the status quo. The United States remains committed to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and the full implementation of all DPRK-related UN Security Council resolutions. Expanding Trade, Energy, and Technology Ties The United States remains ASEAN’s largest single country foreign direct investor, with more than $557 billion in foreign direct investment in the region as of 2025, which supports an estimated 532,000 American jobs. The United States congratulated ASEAN leaders for signing the Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which has the potential to provide U.S. technology companies with greater opportunities in the region’s digital economy projected to reach $2 trillion by 2030. As American Super Intelligence (SI) technology sets the gold standard worldwide, the United States is working with Southeast Asian partners to expand access to U.S. technology, including through the U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK program, which will help unlock the region’s economic potential. By signing the AI Opportunity Statement, Vietnam and Cambodia joined other nations in committing to fostering innovation anchored in trusted partnerships. To support the region’s SI readiness, the United States will collaborate with the Government of Indonesia, ASEAN Secretariat, and Carnegie Mellon University to host ASEAN SI Week in Jakarta in December. The United States and the Philippines signed a five-year Economic Prosperity and Resilience Strategic Objective Agreement, which will mobilize investment in critical infrastructure, including in the Luzon Economic Corridor, and secure supply chains with reliable partners. As one of the world’s largest energy producers, the United States can power Southeast Asia’s growth for generations. The United States is ready to work with ASEAN to strengthen the region’s energy security through support for the ASEAN Power Grid. The United States is sharing its 70 years of experience and leadership in nuclear energy by promoting nuclear safety, security, and nonproliferation in Southeast Asia. Building on our existing 123 Agreements with Indonesia and Vietnam, the United States has entered into 123 Agreements with the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand, and launched negotiations with Malaysia. This cooperation will help the region meet its growing energy demand, including reliable power for SI. The United States is expanding civil nuclear cooperation in Southeast Asia, where energy demand is anticipated to triple by 2050. Consistent with the U.S.-Japan-South Korea Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) on Small Modular Reactor (SMR) deployments, the United States is providing SMR control room simulators and other technical assistance to Indonesia under the Department’s Foundational Infrastructure for the Responsible Use of Small Modular Reactor Technology (FIRST) program to help establish Indonesia as a regional SMR hub. These partnerships strengthen energy security, drive economic growth, and support jobs in the United States and across the region. Combating Scams and Transnational Crime Scam groups based in Southeast Asia stole at least $18.2 billion from Americans and around $23 billion from citizens of ASEAN member states in 2025. In response, President Trump issued Executive Order 14390, titled “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” and the Department of State has confronted these criminal groups head on. The Department is directing an additional $26.2 million to train and equip Southeast Asian law enforcement and criminal justice officials to work with U.S. law enforcement to catch and prosecute scam network operators. The United States and 12 regional partners in the Contact Group to Counter Criminal Online Scams agreed to a Statement of Principles to drive joint action to dismantle the scam syndicates targeting our people. The United States and ASEAN also adopted the U.S.-ASEAN Statement on 10 Public-Private Partnership Principles for Tackling Online Scams, deepening regional and private-sector cooperation.

Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。
夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。
请各位捐助者通过电子邮箱：[email redacted] 与Julia Lee等志愿者联系，以获得相关细节。

content:
谷歌威脅情報小組（GTIG）週四（11月19日）發布報告指出，一個高度活躍中共黑客組織至少兩個月來一直在利用VMware vCenter軟件中的一項重大零日漏洞發動攻擊。示意圖。（shutterstock）
【大紀元2026年11月21日訊】（大紀元記者李平綜合報導）谷歌威脅情報小組（GTIG）週四（11月19日）發布報告指出，一個高度活躍中共黑客組織至少兩個月來一直在利用VMware vCenter軟件中的一項重大零日漏洞發動攻擊。
據美國B2B（企業級）網絡安全新聞與商業分析媒體Cybersecurity Dive報導，該黑客名為Armory Castle，此前被追蹤為UNC5221。黑客利用編號為CVE-2026-123890的漏洞，在受害系統中建立入侵據點、提升權限和竊取敏感數據。
GTIG高級分析師凱莉·范德利（Kelli Vanderlee）表示，目前已確認幾家機構遭到入侵，預計還有其它目標受到影響。
VMware週四當天公布漏洞並發布修補程序，同時警告客戶黑客可利用這一漏洞繞過身分驗證程序，取得受感染系統的管理員控制權，獲得權限後便能執行任意指令、部署專門設計的惡意軟件、竊取用戶憑證和受信任密鑰。
此次攻擊能發生，是Armory Castle曾利用BeyondTrust Remote Support軟件的一項零日漏洞入侵目標系統，此後以此作為初始入口進行後續攻擊。該漏洞編號為CVE-2026-102764，GTIG和網絡安全公司Mandiant今年10月發現的一個網絡間諜行動就是利用這一漏洞，這次間諜活動也是持續近兩個月才被發現。
Armory Castle用於攻擊VMware vCenter漏洞的工具名叫Bonesaw，專門用於遠程入侵、竊取數據庫、劫持身分驗證令牌和創建單點登錄（SSO）管理員帳戶。
此外，Bonesaw的編譯時間比此次入侵行動早一個多月，說明它很可能是提前開發，目的是搞更大範圍的攻擊行動。
網絡安全公司Mandiant Consulting首席技術官查爾斯·卡馬克爾（Charles Carmakal）表示，Bonesaw最早在今年7月被發現。
自2023年以來，GTIG和Mandiant就追蹤到Armory Castle一直利用邊緣網絡設備和安全設備中的零日及已知漏洞發動初始入侵。研究人員指出，Bonesaw的出現，表明Armory Castle已將零日漏洞的利用範圍大幅擴展至成功入侵後的攻擊活動。
Armory Castle使用SAWSNAKE、vmfs_browser.py等專門針對VMware系統的工具，同時部署針對Remote Support設備和Linux系統設計的惡意軟件，形成種類多樣的攻擊工具體系。這些工具針對不同設備量身定製，顯示出Armory Castle對各類目標系統非常了解。
GTIG安全工程師約翰·沃爾夫拉姆（John Wolfram）表示，Armory Castle在一次攻擊行動中使用三套不同的專用惡意軟件和兩個零日漏洞，說明背後有大量資源支持，也說明它為入侵高價值目標投入巨大人力和資源。
此次攻擊再次凸顯，VMware vCenter等虛擬化基礎設施仍是高級持續性威脅（APT）組織重點攻擊的目標。
研究人員表示，Armory Castle在這些攻擊行動上投入大量時間和資源，說明它具備雄厚的技術與資源實力，目的就是持續搜尋目標機構，開展更大規模的網絡間諜活動。
研究人員建議，vCenter是虛擬化數據中心的中央控制平台，僅依靠漏洞出現後再進行修補，已不足以保障安全。企業必須採取主動防禦和零信任策略，強化基礎設施安全，以抵禦現有及尚未被發現的零日漏洞攻擊。
為全面防範APT對虛擬化平台的攻擊，Mandiant強烈建議企業參考《vSphere與BRICKSTORM惡意軟件：防禦人員指南》（vSphere and BRICKSTORM Malware: A Defender's Guide）。
指南詳細介紹了以基礎設施為核心的防禦策略，包括按照安全技術實施指南（STIG）進行安全基準評估、通過特權訪問工作站（PAW）強化身分管理，以及將vCenter設備轉變為主動監測安全威脅的傳感器。
對於受漏洞影響的系統，Mandiant強烈建議企業儘快安裝Broadcom發布的官方安全補丁。

summary: 台湾称中国在 APEC 上的不当待遇不会开创先例 - 焦点台湾 台湾称中国在 APEC 上的不当待遇不会开创先例 要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。中新社台北11月20日电 一名官员周五表示，尽管事先与北京方面进行了谈判，但今年在中国举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)会议期间，台湾遭遇了多起不当待遇事件，但这些事件不会成为先例。中国被选为2024年11月APEC主办国后，台湾开始与北京会谈
content:

中新社台北11月20日电 一名官员周五表示，尽管事先与北京方面进行了谈判，但今年在中国举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)会议期间，台湾遭遇了多起不当待遇事件，但这些事件不会成为先例。
这位官员表示，在中国被选为 2024 年 11 月主办 APEC 会议后，台湾开始与北京进行谈判，以确保作为成员经济体的平等参与以及代表的安全和行动自由。
该官员表示，从那时起到周四在深圳闭幕的APEC领导人非正式会议期间，台北和北京就这些问题进行了17轮谈判，而台湾也寻求志同道合国家的支持来表达自己的关切。
然而，该官员表示，经济部长龚明鑫未能出席9月份在广州举行的亚太经合组织中小企业部长级会议，因为中国以政治理由阻止他参加。
该官员还对APEC领导人非正式会议邀请的发出方式和形式表示不满，但没有提供更多细节。
台湾曾要求中国遵循2014年主办APEC时的安排，包括由中国官员亲自发出邀请。
这位官员表示，北京最终未能满足台湾的期望。
不过，这位官员表示，中国对台湾的不当对待不会开创先例。
据该负责人介绍，今年共有来自25个以上政府部委、机构的400余人赴华参加APEC各级会议。

Taiwan says China's improper treatment at APEC will not set precedent - Focus Taiwan
Taiwan says China's improper treatment at APEC will not set precedent
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 20 (CNA) Taiwan encountered several instances of improper treatment during this year's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meetings in China despite prior negotiations with Beijing, but the incidents will not set a precedent, an official said on Friday.
After China was selected to host APEC in November 2024, Taiwan began talks with Beijing to ensure equal participation as a member economy, and the safety and freedom of movement of its delegates, the official said.
From then until the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting concluded in Shenzhen on Thursday, Taipei and Beijing held 17 rounds of negotiations on these issues, while Taiwan also sought support from like-minded countries to voice its concerns, the official said.
Nevertheless, Economics Minister Kung Ming-hsin (龔明鑫) was unable to attend the APEC Small and Medium Enterprises Ministerial Meeting in Guangzhou in September, as China cited political reasons for preventing him from participating, the official said.
The official also expressed dissatisfaction with how the invitation to the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting was delivered and its format, without providing further details.
Taiwan had asked China to follow the arrangements used in 2014, when it last hosted APEC, including having a Chinese official personally deliver the invitation.
Beijing ultimately failed to meet Taiwan's expectations, the official said.
However, the official said China's improper treatment of Taiwan would not set a precedent.
According to the official, more than 400 people from over 25 government ministries and agencies traveled to China this year to take part in APEC meetings at various levels.

# 欧洲各地爆发了抗议活动 ，高喊： “为我们的未来而战，而不是为他们的战争而战”

欧洲 –  周五，欧洲各地爆发了抗议活动。从高昂的生活成本到军费开支，再到气候危机， 示威者表达了他们的不满。他们向各国领导人施加了更大压力，指责这些领导人无视年轻人的诉求。工会、各类协会及青年组织号召在11月20日、21日和22日开展为期三天的系列行动。口号是：“为我们的未来而战，而非为他们的战争而战。”

发表时间： 20/11/2026 - 22:18

 9 分钟 浏览时间

 2026年11月20日，意大利博洛尼亚街头的示威活动 © Massimiliano Donati / Getty Images

 作者： [安东尼](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%9C%E5%B0%BC/ "安东尼")

广告

继续浏览后续

法新社报道，在意大利、德国、奥地利和英国等国的多个城市，示威者走上街头。许多人挥舞着写有“为我们的未来而战”字样的标语，现场有人燃放信号弹，还有人焚烧了纸板制作的坦克模型。

这些抗议活动由一个以年轻人为主导、涵盖50多个团体的联盟共同组织。示威者不满的原因包括以色列在加沙地带的战争、高昂的租金，以及学校和大学日益恶化的学习环境。

法新社说，这些抗议活动有着一个共同的主题：人们认为，欧洲各国的政府忙于应对地缘政治危机并扶持大企业，却在保障年轻一代福祉方面投入不足。

在意大利米兰的一场抗议活动中，18岁的高中生奥利维亚·费拉里奥（Olivia Ferrario）表示，年轻人通过走上街头，展现出了他们的“活力与决心”。

她说，“如果政府不倾听我们的声音，我们就不能保持沉默”。

由于担心之前在法国及其他国家大规模抗议活动中曾出现的街头暴力事件重演，这次警方已部署了大量警力。

在柏林，约有1000名大学生和中学生举行了抗议活动，表达了他们对德国迅速扩军等问题的担忧这种扩军趋势引发了人们对于恢复强制兵役制的恐惧。

“在我看来，强迫他人学习如何战斗和杀人，然后再把他们送上战场……这根本是毫无道理的，”去年刚高中毕业的18岁学生海伦娜·科萨茨（Helena Kossatz）在接受法新社采访时表示。

在欧洲因面对敌对的俄罗斯而寻求扩军的时候，这些遍及欧洲各地的抗议活动的组织者认为，原本用于扩军的资金，应当投入到教育、青年政策和住房建设中。

在伦敦，几百名抗议者聚集在议会大厦外及附近的特拉法加广场，他们举着标语牌，上面写着“拯救高等教育”以及“为我们的未来而奋斗，而不是为他们的战争而战”。

18岁的学生埃利兹是大学生， 她对法新社说，不确定自己是否还能上大学，“因为钱的问题。而且，大多数工作正逐渐被人工智能取代。大家普遍感到更加压抑了。”

现场还发生了右翼抗议者与反法西斯抗议者之间的肢体冲突。

在伦敦的抗议活动中，有人高呼“巴勒斯坦永存”的口号；在欧洲各地的多场抗议活动中，也都能见到巴勒斯坦国旗。

在罗马，一群高中生打着横幅游行，横幅上写道：“如果没人给我们自由，那我们就自己去争取——反对政府、反对战争、反对高昂的生活成本。”

现场也发生了冲突，一些抗议者向警察投掷了瓶子和烟雾弹。

在西班牙首都马德里，抗议者们呼吁增加教育经费，并强烈反对增加军费开支。

16岁的高中生塞拉诺表示，她所在的班级有33名学生，却只有一名老师。

“教室非常狭小，设施状况极其糟糕，”她说道，有些学校甚至有老鼠和蟑螂。

抗议活动预计将持续到周末，工会和住房协会已号召举行进一步的示威活动。

法国也计划于周六举行示威活动。此次抗议活动正值法国“黄马甲”运动周年纪念之际；黄马甲运动曾在2018年和2019年让法国总统马克龙深感不安。

欧洲多国的抗议活动在一定程度上受到了近期法国示威活动的影响，而法国的这些示威有时演变成了暴力事件。

这一系列抗议始于9月中旬，当时法国的学生们在各所高中举行示威，要求改善学习环境；随后，这场运动演变为一场全国性的抗议浪潮，反对物价飞涨、反对公共服务不足，反对警察暴力行为。
