title: Tackling doubt and distrust: Taiwan cracks down on disinformation ahead of local elections
zh_title: 消除疑虑和不信任：台湾在地方选举前打击虚假信息
summary: 消除疑虑和不信任：台湾在地方选举前打击虚假信息 |海峡时报 消除疑虑和不信任：台湾在地方选举前打击虚假信息 立即注册：了解亚洲快速发展的情况 10 月中旬，一名台湾政客在社交媒体上发帖暗示，支持民进党台北市长候选人沉普马的网上海报是有偿宣传。发表于 2026 年 11 月 20 日下午 05:00 更新于 2026 年 11 月 20 日下午 09:24 台湾表示，来自中国的虚假信息和网络攻击在 11 月 28 日之前正在增加
content:
消除疑虑和不信任：台湾在地方选举前打击虚假信息 |海峡时报
消除疑虑和不信任：台湾在地方选举前打击虚假信息
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
10月中旬，一名台湾政客在社交媒体上发帖暗示，网上支持民进党台北市长候选人沉彪马的海报是有偿宣传的。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 20 日，下午 05:00
更新于 2026 年 11 月 20 日 09:24
台湾表示，在 11 月 28 日地方选举之前，来自中国的虚假信息和网络攻击正在增加。截至 11 月 16 日，警方已处理 251 起选举虚假信息案件。
虚假帖子通过抹黑、虚假民意调查和深度伪造来针对候选人。官员们表示，外国势力和人工智能让谎言传播得更快、更难追踪、也更有说服力。
专家警告说，这样做的目的是散布怀疑、恐惧和不信任，而不仅仅是帮助一位候选人。这可能会让选民感到疲倦、分裂，并对民主失去信心。
台北 — — 台湾国家安全局在 10 月份向立法院提交的一份报告中表示，2026 年前 9 个月，检测到超过 250 万条来自中国的争议性在线信息，比上年增加约 48%。
与此同时，自6月份以来，中共针对台湾政府的网络攻击次数也稳步上升，7月份检测到的总数已超过1亿次。
随着 11 月 28 日地方选举临近，台湾警察厅 (NPA) 警告称，包括深度造假在内的更多选举虚假信息可能会浮出水面。它可以来自台湾境内，也可以来自台湾境外。
截至11月16日，台湾警方已查处选举虚假信息案件251起，其中145起案件涉及193名台湾籍嫌疑人，司法机关正在进一步调查中。
最常见的选举虚假信息类型涉及诽谤候选人及其同事。其他包括捏造民意调查；冒充政府机构、媒体或候选人；提供误导性投票信息；刑事调查局表示，散布有关选举舞弊的谣言。
该公司在 11 月 18 日的一份声明中表示：“此类内容可以通过社交媒体平台和消息应用程序迅速传播，通常采用耸人听闻的标题、经过处理的图像或人工智能生成的音频和视频来误导公众。”
该机构还强调，10 月和 11 月病例数量迅速增加。
新人民军副局长郭世杰在11月4日举行的选举虚假信息新闻发布会上表示：“我们还发现，有外国势力依靠传播虚假信息，甚至利用跨国镇压来干扰选举。”
当被问及选举虚假信息是否源自中国时，郭表示很难确定，因为肇事者使用 VPN 或虚拟专用网络等方法来掩盖他们的踪迹。
内华达大学拉斯维加斯分校政治学系副教授奥斯汀·王表示，中国的内容农场可能会在平时发布有关其他事项的内容，例如与健康相关的问题，但会“在需要时突然谈论中国叙事”。
他告诉《海峡时报》：“在 2024 年和 2022 年的上一次选举中，我们……注意到选举前的叙述和语气发生了类似的转变。”
NPA 指出

【原文 English Original】
Tackling doubt and distrust: Taiwan cracks down on disinformation ahead of local elections | The Straits Times
Tackling doubt and distrust: Taiwan cracks down on disinformation ahead of local elections
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
A social media post in mid-October by a Taiwan politician insinuated that online posters supporting Democratic Progressive Party candidate for Taipei mayor Puma Shen were paid propaganda.
Published Nov 20, 2026, 05:00 PM
Updated Nov 20, 2026, 09:24 PM
Taiwan says disinformation and cyberattacks from China are rising before the Nov 28 local elections. Police had handled 251 election disinformation cases by Nov 16.
False posts target candidates with smears, fake polls and deepfakes. Officials say foreign forces and AI make the lies faster, harder to trace and more convincing.
Experts warn that the goal is to spread doubt, fear and distrust, not just help one candidate. This can make voters tired, divided and less confident in democracy.
TAIPEI – More than 2.5 million controversial online messages from China were detected in the first nine months of 2026, an increase of around 48% over the previous year, said Taiwan’s National Security Bureau in a report to the Legislative Yuan in October.
At the same time, the number of cyberattacks by the Communist Party of China against the Taiwanese government has also been rising steadily since June, with the total number detected in July exceeding 100 million, the bureau added.
And as the Nov 28 local elections near, Taiwan’s National Police Agency (NPA) has warned that more election disinformation, including deepfakes, is likely to surface. And it can come from both within Taiwan and beyond its shores.
As at Nov 16, Taiwan’s police agencies had handled 251 cases of election disinformation, of which 145 cases involving 193 Taiwanese suspects are being investigated further by judicial authorities.
The most common type of election disinformation involved smearing the candidates and their associates. Others include fabricating opinion polls; impersonating government agencies, media outlets or candidates; providing misleading voting information; and spreading rumours about election fraud, said the Criminal Investigation Bureau.
“Such content can spread rapidly via social media platforms and messaging apps, often employing sensational headlines, manipulated images, or AI-generated audio and video to mislead the public,” it said in a statement on Nov 18.
The agency also highlighted that the number of cases has risen rapidly in October and November.
“We have also found that there are foreign forces relying on the spread of disinformation, and even using transnational repression to interfere with the elections,” said NPA’s deputy director-general Kuo Shih-Chieh at a press briefing on election disinformation on Nov 4.
When asked if the election disinformation originated from China, Kuo said it was hard to determine as perpetrators use methods such as VPNs, or virtual private networks, to mask their tracks.
Austin Wang, associate professor at the Department of Political Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas, said that China-based content farms may post content about other matters, such as health-related issues, on normal days, but will “suddenly talk about Chinese narratives when needed”.
“In the previous elections in 2024 and 2022, we… noticed a similar shift in narrative and tone right before the election,” he told The Straits Times.
The NPA noted that there have been more fake controversial posts being spread online, even if they are not related to the election.
For such messages, a high proportion come from overseas IP addresses and have increased significantly in 2026.
“They may not be directly related to the election, but they are clearly false information intended to sow doubt in the public about the government and the democratic system,” said Kuo.
There are online fan pages for sports, movies or other hobbies that appear about six months before the election, which then surreptitiously post political messages as the election draws near, political scientist Chen Fang-yu said at a forum on Oct 28.
While disagreements are common between different political camps in a democracy, Chen, an associate professor at Taiwan’s Soochow University, said disinformation posts will use personal attacks and provocative messages to exacerbate these differences.
A controversial “movie poster” depicting Chiang Wan-an from the Beijing-friendly Kuomintang party as a gun-toting “hero” eliminating “three evils”: his opponents from the Democratic Progressive Party and the Social Democratic Party. Chiang’s campaign office filed a police report and issued an urgent clarification on Oct 28, stating that the image was not created or released by them.
Disinformation is not always intended to encourage people to vote for a certain candidate, experts said. It could even come in the form of “fake support”.
Puma Shen from the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) is one example. He was raved about in online posters splashed across Facebook fan pages in mid-October, with slogans such as “Yang wave unleashes its power!”.
A pun on Shen’s Chinese name Shen Pao-yang, “Yang wave” refers to his rising popularity that has seemingly swept Taipei this election. Shen is running against incumbent Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an from the Beijing-friendly Kuomintang (KMT) party.
Criticising the posters, Taipei city councillor Hou Han-ting, from the New Party, said: “It’s New Taiwan Dollars and online trolls unleashing their power”, implying they were paid propaganda from Shen’s own campaign rather than true support for the DPP candidate.
Puma Shen’s debut in Taipei mayoral election creates more than waves. But can it translate to votes?
Can KMT’s Chiang Wan-an rally supporters in tight mayor race to defend his Taipei seat?
Taiwanese media later reported that a cybersecurity expert who examined the fan pages found that they originated not from Shen’s campaign but from the Borderless Group, a content farm in Qinhuangdao, Hebei province in north China.
The Chinese group usually posts sensational stories to attract eyeballs, but with local elections in Taiwan heating up, it is jumping on the election bandwagon.
But here’s the irony: Shen, a criminologist, has helped raise awareness of Chinese influence operations. Even before he ran for mayor, China’s Taiwan Affairs Office designated him a “diehard separatist” – a label Beijing reserves for those in Taiwan’s pro-independence movement it considers the most extreme.
Beijing even placed a trade ban on the trading company owned by Shen’s father, barring it from all dealings with mainland firms and individuals.
The cybersecurity expert’s discovery then raises the question: Why would a Chinese content farm impersonate Shen’s fans and put up posts promoting him?
The aim could be to make them lose faith in the democratic system, said Chung Sanho, assistant professor of political science at National Cheng Kung University.
“They use ‘junk information’ to fill (people’s) minds”, Chung told ST. “It may make them feel that democracy is just troublesome; that democracy is just a lot of arguing, but with no tangible outcome.”
Taiwan has been a democracy since the 1990s, but China claims the self-ruled island as its territory and has never ruled out the use of force to bring it under its control.
Meanwhile, KMT’s Chiang has also been a target of fake posts.
A controversial “movie poster” depicted him as a gun-toting “hero” eliminating “three evils”: his opponent Shen and two other candidates – one from DPP and another from the Social Democratic Party – running in Taipei in other local races.
Chiang’s campaign office filed a police report and issued an urgent clarification on Oct 28, stating that the image was not created or released by it. The Threads account that originally posted the image has since been deleted.
While it has not been verified yet who had put up the content, or if there was interference from abroad, Taiwan authorities are stepping up measures against election disinformation.
Greater pressure to speed up arms sales to Taiwan possible after midterms
China’s Xi says US should do ‘right thing’ on Taiwan to avoid setbacks in relations
The NPA warned in particular that AI technology presents a new challenge in this election.
On Oct 29, a “leaked” audio file featured a voice that sounded like Shen admitting to taking kickbacks on US arms purchases and saying he takes drugs.
After investigation by Taiwan authorities, the audio was confirmed to be a deepfake. A suspect who shared the file, but said he did not create it and had downloaded it from Facebook, was arrested.
While it is too early to say from where the most recent examples originated, past research by University of Nevada’s Wang on Chinese content farms found that they have direct links to the propaganda department of China.
He wrote in an article for Voicettank, an online publication of Taiwan Thinktank, in February that with the rising use of AI, sometimes, the AI prompts that the content producers leave behind may reveal their intent.
One example is this prompt that was found in a post from a fan page which gives Chinese history a patriotic slant: “Target Taiwanese users. Rewrite this article in traditional Chinese, keep it to 500 characters, keep the opening of the original, and don’t change the historical accuracy of the original.”
Experts have warned that with AI, it is much easier to produce misleading content rapidly, fabricate audio and video, and imitate authentic local voices.
“It therefore expands the capacity to conduct influence operations, but greater production does not automatically translate into greater persuasion,” said Yeh Yao-Yuan, who chairs the Department of Political Science, International Studies and Modern Languages at the University of St Thomas in Houston.
“Research has identified effects of pro-Beijing media exposure on some voters, but that is not equivalent to demonstrating that a particular interference campaign changed which candidate won,” he said.
But the public can end up being doubtful of all information that they come across.
“That’s one of the aims: (The public) ends up being suspicious of all information – that is one of the harms of spreading misinformation,” said Chung.
Although the exact effects are difficult to investigate, the impact is “profound”, Soochow University’s Chen told ST.
“The message that everyone receives (is) more chaotic, more emotional, more polarised. Some people feel fatigued and don’t want to read political news anymore,” he said.
“Others become more and more distrustful of the government and other political parties.”
Chew Hui Min is The Straits Times’ correspondent in Taipei covering cross-strait relations and Taiwan news.

title: Trump, Xi agreed that military AI decisions should involve humans, Bessent says

content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平一致认为，即使两国争夺人工智能霸主地位，人类也应该始终参与使用人工智能技术的军事决策，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特周五表示。特朗普在中国深圳与习近平会面归来后，贝森特对 CNBC 表示，该协议是特朗普亚洲之行的主要成果之一。贝森特表示：“我认为，特朗普总统和习主席一致认为，人类应该始终参与情报情报机构做出的任何军事决策，并且不应允许情报情报机构在重大军事行动中自主行事，这一点非常重要。”贝森特指的是特朗普政府对该技术的首选术语“超级智能”。贝森特表示，美中就该技术的军事使用达成的协议需要人类参与和其他保障措施，不会受到两国人工智能霸主竞争的影响。他补充说，美国人工智能实验室需要保持其技术领先地位，作为抵御网络攻击中使用的“危险”中国人工智能模型的最佳防御手段。贝森特说：“但是，当双方都同意不应该在无人参与的情况下发起任何重大军事行动时，这与竞争无关。”
他表示，涉及英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋和一名与他有恋情的中国公民的间谍指控并未在特习双边会晤中提及。贝森特表示，在特朗普采取他所谓的“非常强硬的路线”后，英伟达的第二级人工智能芯片 H200 仍然是中国可以通过许可购买的最先进的芯片。 “我认为我们看到的是中国人在 H200 上的订单很少，因为他们试图构建自己的芯片堆栈，而且我认为他们可能落后了很多年，”他补充道。英伟达丑闻发生后，贝森特淡化了财政部长和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克在人工智能芯片限制问题上所表达的分歧，称特朗普政府官员“都致力于遵循特朗普总统的指示”。美国商务部周一采取措施，进一步限制中国获得先进人工智能芯片，包括中国实体可以租用计算能力的海外数据中心使用的芯片。 “我认为我们将会看到适当的芯片限制已经到位，并且远程访问已经被限制，”他说。

【原文 English Original】
President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed humans should always be involved in military decisions that use artificial intelligence technologies, even as the two countries compete for AI supremacy , Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday. Bessent told CNBC after returning from Trump’s meeting with Xi in Shenzhen, China, that the agreement was among the major achievements of Trump’s trip to Asia. “I think it was very important that President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” Bessent said, referring to the Trump administration’s preferred term for the technology, “super intelligence.” Bessent said that the U.S.-China agreement on military use of the technology, requiring human involvement and other safeguards, would not be affected by the two countries’ competition for AI supremacy. He added that U.S. AI labs needed to maintain their technological lead as the best defense against “dangerous” Chinese AI models that are being used in cyberattacks. “But there’s nothing to do with competition when it says that both sides agree that no major military operation should be launched without a human being involved,” Bessent said. He said that the spying allegations involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese national that he was romantically involved with did not come up in the Trump-Xi bilateral meeting. Bessent said that Nvidia’s second-tier AI chip, the H200, remained the most advanced chip that China could purchase with licenses, after Trump took what he called a “very firm line.” “I think what we have seen is a paucity of orders from the Chinese on the H200s as they try to build out their own chip stack, and I think that they are probably many years behind,” he added. Bessent downplayed differences that he had voiced between the views of Treasury and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on AI chip restrictions in the wake of the Nvidia scandal, saying Trump administration officials were “all committed to following President Trump’s instructions.” The Commerce Department took steps on Monday to further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips, including those used by overseas data centers where Chinese entities can rent computing power. “I think we are going to see that the proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed,” he said.

This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family

Takaichi to meet ICC president on Tuesday
International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane | jiji

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will meet with Tomoko Akane, president of the International Criminal Court, at the prime minister’s office in Tokyo on Tuesday, the government said Friday.
Takaichi and Akane will meet for the first time since the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump added the ICC president to its sanctions list in August. The meeting aims to send a message to the international community that Japan continues to fully support the ICC.
The prime minister last met Akane in January.
In response to the sanctions, Japan plans to make an early payment of its assessed contribution to the ICC for 2027. Takaichi is expected to outline such support measures during the meeting with Akane.
On Tuesday, Akane is also due to give a lecture at an event hosted by the Nonpartisan Parliamentary Association for Reconsidering Human Rights Diplomacy.

title: The military lacks an ‘overarching plan’ to improve munition stockpiles—partly because it’s no one’s job
zh_title: 军方缺乏改善弹药库存的“总体计划”——部分原因是这不是任何人的工作
summary: 根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军队可以购买的东西和实际需要的东西之间的差异。
content:
根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军方可以购买的东西与实际需要的东西之间存在差异，政府问责局表示，这甚至可能导致弹药投资超出五角大楼的要求。该报告的作者写道：“虽然国防部正在采取措施关注弹药短缺问题，但它无法解决这些差距。” “国防部没有总体计划，也没有指定和授权的领导层来改善弹药库存并满足其弹药需求。由于没有确定长期目标、实现这些目标的战略以及衡量进展的指标，国防部无法确定其行动能否解决弹药短缺问题。”包括国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在内的高级政府官员否认美国存在弹药短缺，尽管有报告和独立分析显示，伊朗冲突已经严重耗尽了弹药。关键武器，特别是备受追捧的爱国者拦截机，其制造时间可能超过两年。
但在对政府问责局研究的回应中，五角大楼官员同意军方需要制定一项长期计划来提高弹药生产的建议。五角大楼负责采购的代理副手大卫·卡德曼写道：“我们同意需要一个总体框架，更好地整合弹药需求、库存水平、生产、资源和长期目标。”他补充说，国防部“已经执行了政府问责局建议中的许多内容”。美国政府问责局的研究并未探讨特定弹药的库存，而是研究了五角大楼跟踪、预测和总体处理一系列武器（从炮弹到战斧导弹）的过程。 “重要的是，[这项研究]与当前的短缺无关，”战略与国际研究中心的高级顾问马克·坎西恩（Mark Cancian）撰写了大量有关弹药政策的文章。 “这关系到未来并决定长期库存、生产和弹药组合。”  国防官员强调需要“高低”弹药组合，即高科技、难以制造的武器和廉价武器之间的平衡。伊朗战争说明了美军对昂贵拦截机的依赖，这些拦截机投入了大量资金来击落廉价的沙赫德无人机，这些无人机的成本只有数万美元。
彭博资讯国防分析师韦恩·桑德斯表示：“当你拥有先进的能力，并且开始消耗先进的能力来击落快速补充的非先进能力时，这是一场我们赢不了的经济游戏。”“这开始转变为军事领域的一场革命，表明我们必须改变我们的学说，同时改变我们在美国的生产能力。”   美国政府问责局国防能力主管戴安娜·摩尔达夫斯基 (Diana Moldafsky) 在周五发给《防务一号》的一封电子邮件中指出，五角大楼已经发现了不足之处

【原文 English Original】
The Defense Department has no “overarching plan” to identify, achieve, or measure its progress toward long-term munition production goals, according to a Government Accountability Office study released on Thursday, which said the military was too reactive to global events and unprepared to forecast its own needs. The GAO cited—among other issues—a lack of centralized authority over weapons inventories, which have been depleted by the Iran war and are vital to U.S. plans for a potential conflict with China. At the center of the problem lies a discrepancy between what the military can buy and what it actually needs, which the GAO said could even result in munition investments that exceed the Pentagon’s requirements.  “While DOD is taking steps to focus on munitions shortages, it is not positioned to address these gaps,” the report’s authors wrote. “DOD does not have an overarching plan or designated and empowered leadership to improve munition inventories and meet its munitions requirements. By not identifying long-term goals, strategies to achieve them, and metrics to gauge progress, DOD cannot be sure that its actions will address its munition shortfalls. ” Top administration officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have denied that the U.S. has a shortage in munitions, despite reports and independent analyses showing the Iran conflict has alarmingly drained key weapons, especially for highly-sought Patriot interceptors that can take more than two years to make. But in its response to the GAO study, Pentagon officials concurred with the recommendation that the military needed to develop a long-term plan to improve its munition production.  “We agree with the need for an overarching framework that better integrates munition requirements, inventory levels, production, resources, and long-term objectives,” wrote David Cadman, the Pentagon’s acting deputy for acquisitions, who added that the department “already executes many elements” of the GAO’s recommendation. The GAO study did not explore the inventories of specific munitions, but examined the processes by which an expansive list of weapons — from artillery shells to Tomahawk missiles — are tracked, forecast and generally addressed by the Pentagon. “The important thing is that [the study] is not about current shortages,” Mark Cancian, a senior adviser with the Center for Strategic and International Studies who has written extensively on munitions policy. “It's about the future and deciding long-term inventories, production, and munitions mixes.”  Defense officials have emphasized the need for a “high-low” mix of munitions—that is, a balance between high-tech, hard-to-make weapons and cheaper ones. The Iran war illustrated the U.S. military’s reliance on expensive interceptors, which were heavily expended to shoot down cheap Shahed drones that only cost tens of thousands of dollars.  “When you have an exquisite capacity, and you are starting to expend an exquisite capacity to knock down non-exquisite capabilities that are rapidly replenished, it is an economical game that we're not going to win,” said Wayne Sanders, a defense analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence. “This is starting to turn into one of those revolutions in military affairs to say we have to change our doctrine as well as we change our production capacity in the U.S.”   In an email to Defense One on Friday, the GAO’s director for defense capabilities, Diana Moldafsky, noted that the Pentagon had identified shortfalls before the conflict with Iran, but said that the war “made addressing those shortages more urgent.” “Our key point is that meeting DOD's munitions requirements will be challenging,” Moldafsky said. “A department-wide plan would help the department direct its resources towards its most critical munitions needs.”  Cancian said that Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the consequent transfer of Patriots and other weapons to Kyiv, introduced concerns about the defense industrial base and its ability to respond to munition needs around the world. Meanwhile, the Pentagon has inked billions of dollars in multi-year “framework agreements” with top defense companies over the last year to help increase high-tech munition production, which require funding from Congress to come to fruition. The Trump administration also invoked the Defense Production Act earlier this year in an attempt to bolster munition supply chains. A Pentagon spokesperson declined to address the GAO study directly, or even to be quoted by name. But they said the military is “fully equipped to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing…while preserving a deep, ready stockpile to defend our people and interests.” Part of the problem is that no one authority is really in charge of keeping arsenals topped off and ready, the report found.  The GAO identified several Pentagon offices and working groups, including individual service entities, responsible for managing munition inventories, but no one dedicated authority “that empowers the leadership to make decisions that improve munitions inventories department-wide and hold them accountable for the outcomes achieved, such as improving munitions inventory levels.” The study also said that the services maintain separate tools to track munition inventories, which then feed into a Pentagon system known as the Munitions Readiness Initiative. But researchers said the DOD has limited oversight over that tracking platform and hasn’t regularly reconciled it with service-level numbers. Citing an unnamed Pentagon official in its acquisitions and sustainment office, the GAO said “the office was reluctant to impose additional responsibilities on the services for maintaining data to meet MRI’s needs because they recognize that the services already face numerous responsibilities in managing their own munitions inventory data.” The Pentagon concurred with most of the GAO’s recommendations, but only partially agreed with one: that the data management plan be run out of the DOD’s digital and AI office. Cadman’s response said that the Pentagon’s acquisition and sustainment arm was best suited to develop it. ]]>

美國總統川普（右）、中國國家主席習近平（中）和俄羅斯總統普丁（左）19日展開歷史性的美中俄三方領袖會談。（路透社）
（中央社台北20日電）美中俄元首昨天在深圳舉行歷史性三方會談，外界對於中國國家主席習近平坐在中間，美俄元首分別坐在兩旁有不同解讀。有專家認為，這樣的座位安排顯然不足以確立新的國際秩序，但所呈現的畫面，卻是北京希望外界想像的面貌。
美中俄元首昨天在深圳舉行歷史性會談，根據電視畫面，作為東道主的習近平坐在一張大圓桌的中間，兩旁是美國總統川普（Donald Trump）與俄羅斯總統普丁（Vladimir Putin）；中國國旗也放在三國國旗的中間。
香港南華早報今天報導，專家們對於這樣的座位安排有不同解讀。拜登政府時期任職白宮與國務院中國政策高級官員的葛維茲（Julian Gewirtz）表示，這樣的座位安排呈現一個以中國為中心秩序的畫面，一個由習近平主持的「準G3」集團；而美國總統作為兩位嘉賓之一，出席了由北京召集的世界會議。
不過，葛維茲表示，這樣的座位安排顯然不足以確立新的國際秩序，但所呈現的畫面，卻是北京希望外界想像的面貌。
華府智庫「中美研究中心」（Institute for China-America Studies）資深研究員古普塔（Sourabh Gupta）表示，在座位安排上，主人家享有中間位置是必然的，「與其說是其他原因，不如說是反映他們缺乏信心」。
古普塔又表示，中方選擇圓桌而非三角桌，其實帶有釋放某種訊號的意味，也是刻意安排的，因為三角桌呈現「多中心」的畫面。
古普塔表示，雖然中國起初對於舉行美中俄三方會談的態度猶豫，因為中國向來傾向將國際事務維持在雙邊架構內，且在會前表現得最不積極，但最終結果卻對中國有利。（編輯：陳鎧妤/朱建陵）1151120

（中央社台北20日電）據中國央視新聞報導，北京時間11月18日至20日，中美兩軍於中國上海舉行了2026年度中美海上軍事安全磋商機制第二次工作小組會議和年度會晤。
報導指出，會議旨在落實兩國元首重要共識，推動兩軍關係健康、穩定、可持續發展。雙方就當前中美海空安全形勢進行了坦誠、務實、建設性的交流，評估了「中美海空相遇安全行為準則」年度執行情況，討論了改進中美海上軍事安全問題的措施，並商定了2027年工作小組會議議題。
美國太平洋司令部也發布消息稱，中國海軍接待了美國太平洋司令部的代表，並舉行了半年一次的軍事海上協商協議工作小組和全體會議。
據指出，2026年11月18日至20日，美國太平洋司令部、美國太平洋艦隊、美國太平洋空軍、美國海岸防衛隊的軍事官員，以及美國戰爭部政策副部長辦公室的代表，在上海與中國海軍代表舉行了軍事海上協商協議工作小組會議。該論壇旨在促進相關人員就降低不安全和不專業遭遇的風險進行討論。（編輯：朱建陵/田瑞華）1151120

卫星图像显示，中国浦城有一架不寻常的无人驾驶飞机，其配置与波音公司的舰载 MQ-25 Stingray 非常相似。虽然我们仍然不知道无人机的功能，但该设施本身似乎也成为中国不断扩大的无人驾驶飞机工业的一个日益重要的枢纽。 Vantor 向 TWZ 提供的一张广角卫星图像显示了 2026 年 4 月 23 日在蒲城的神秘无人机。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 这架无人机最初引起了人们的关注，因为它在中国西北部陕西省蒲城内府机场的卫星图像中被发现，可通过苹果地图查看。无人机出现在跑道上的单独图像也可以通过必应地图获得。 TWZ 随后从 Vantor 获得了浦城的图像，显​​示了相关无人驾驶飞机。真是一个惊喜！苹果地图上发现三架无人机出现在浦城。 CH-7、九天和类似MQ-25的无人机。 pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) 2026 年 11 月 18 日再次出现在 bing 地图上！这次它出现在跑道上 pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) 2026 年 11 月 19 日 除了不明飞行器之外，今年 4 月从蒲城拍摄的图像还揭示了似乎是 CH-7 隐形飞翼无人机和重型喷气动力九天母舰无人机的例子。 2026 年 4 月 23 日，一架 CH-7 停泊在蒲城。
卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 2026 年 4 月 23 日在蒲城的九天无人机母舰。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 与不明飞行器最明显的比较是波音的 MQ-25 Stingray。 MQ-25是一种舰载无人飞机，主要为美国海军飞机提供空中加油，扩大舰载机联队的航程和操作灵活性。它还为未来无人海军航空能力奠定了基础。范托称，就尺寸而言，这架身份不明的中国无人机翼展约为66英尺，长度为49英尺。相比之下，MQ-25 的翼展约为 75 英尺，长度约为 51 英尺。 MQ-25 黄貂鱼。波音公司的这款中国无人机似乎具有相似的总体设计类别，但现阶段存在一些值得注意的重要差异。最引人注目的之一是前机身。与MQ-25不同，MQ-25的前部具有相对扁平的铲状外观，中国飞机似乎有一个更传统的锥形机头。也许这可以包含一个容纳雷达设备的锥形天线罩。这个理论，而且它只是一个理论，可以通过机头与黄色底漆机身的不同颜色来支持。进气量也不同。
与 MQ-25 相关的异国情调的齐平进气道不同，中国设计有一个更传统的背部进气道，看起来呈锯齿状，有助于雷达信号和/或分成两个通道。另一种可能性是飞机有两个发动机，尽管基于明显的分叉进气道，这仍然是推测性的。左侧浦城图像中的无人机和 MQ-25 的并排视图，提供了它们入口的比较视图。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor/Boeing 尾部配置也可能很独特，具有横向展开的 V 型尾翼，如 MQ-25，但可能采用可见控制面，而不是全移动水平尾翼设计。综合起来，这些功能

【原文 English Original】
Satellite imagery has revealed an unusual uncrewed aircraft at Pucheng, China, with a configuration that bears very strong similarities to Boeing’s carrier-based MQ-25 Stingray . While we still have no idea about the function of the drone, the facility itself also appears to be an increasingly important hub for China’s expanding uncrewed aircraft industry . A wider-view satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor shows the mystery drone at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The drone initially attracted attention after being spotted in a satellite image of Pucheng Neifu Airport in Shaanxi Province, in northwestern China, available through Apple Maps. A separate image of the drone, where it appears on a runway, is also available through Bing Maps. TWZ subsequently obtained imagery of Pucheng from Vantor showing the uncrewed aircraft in question. what a suprise! Three UAV spotted at Pucheng on apple maps. CH-7, Jiutian and a MQ-25 like UAV. pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 18, 2026 spotted again on bing maps! and it's on the runway this time pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 19, 2026 As well as the unidentified aircraft, imagery from Pucheng dating from April of this year also reveals what appears to be a CH-7 stealthy flying-wing drone and an example of the heavyweight jet-powered Jiutian mothership drone . A CH-7 at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor A Jiutian drone mothership at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The most obvious comparison for the unidentified aircraft is Boeing’s MQ-25 Stingray. The MQ-25 is a carrier-based uncrewed aircraft developed primarily to provide aerial refueling for U.S. Navy aircraft, extending the range and operational flexibility of carrier air wings. It also provides a foundation for future uncrewed naval aviation capabilities . In terms of dimensions, the unidentified Chinese UAV has a wingspan of approximately 66 feet and a length of 49 feet, according to Vantor. In contrast, the MQ-25 measures approximately 75 feet in wingspan and 51 feet in length. MQ-25 Stingray. Boeing The Chinese drone appears to occupy a similar general design category, but there are several important differences notable at this stage. One of the most noticeable is the forward fuselage. Unlike the MQ-25, whose forward section has a relatively flattened, shovel-like appearance, the Chinese aircraft appears to have a more conventional, tapered nose. Perhaps this could incorporate a conical radome housing radar equipment. That theory, and it is just a theory, could be supported by the different color of the nose compared to the yellow primer-painted airframe. The air intake is also different. Rather than the exotic, flush inlet associated with the MQ-25 , the Chinese design has a more conventional dorsal intake that appears serrated to help with radar signature and/or split into two channels. Another possibility is that the aircraft has two engines, although that remains speculative, based on the apparent bifurcated intake. A side-by-side look at the drone seen in the image of Pucheng, at left, and an MQ-25, offering comparative views of their inlets. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/Boeing The tail configuration may also be distinctive, with a laterally flared V-tail, like the MQ-25, but possibly incorporating visible control surfaces instead of an all-moving tailplane design. Taken together, these features suggest an aircraft that shares some of the MQ-25’s general design philosophy but is not an attempt at a direct clone. Long-time Chinese aerospace observer and TWZ contributor Andreas Rupprecht , who has been following developments surrounding the aircraft, believes China could be following a development path similar to Boeing’s, potentially producing a carrier-based uncrewed aerial refueling platform that can also undertake intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. “I think China is actually following the same path as Boeing here, and it’s heading towards a tanker that can also take on other roles as an ISR platform,” Rupprecht told us. A radar-equipped aircraft with substantial endurance could potentially perform surveillance and other sensor-related missions when not being used as a tanker. The potential development of a multirole uncrewed tanker at Pucheng would also fit into a much broader push by China to expand the role of uncrewed aircraft in its naval aviation forces. One of the most notable developments is the GJ-21 , a navalized derivative of the GJ-11 Sharp Sword stealth uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV). Featuring folding wings and provisions for catapult launches and arrested recoveries, the low-observable flying-wing design is intended to operate from China’s growing fleet of large-deck warships , including the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . In October 2026, Chinese state media reported that the GJ-21 had successfully completed its first takeoff and landing aboard the vessel, a significant milestone in the development of shipborne fixed-wing combat drones. GJ-21 carrier-based UCAV. via Chinese internet The GJ-21 effort is taking place alongside the introduction of China’s new catapult-equipped Fujian aircraft carrier, which has begun operating the J-35 stealth fighter, J-15T carrier-based fighter, and KJ-600 airborne early warning aircraft. Taken together, these developments point to an increasingly ambitious effort to integrate uncrewed aircraft into China’s future carrier air wings , potentially spanning stealthy strike platforms, surveillance systems, and other specialized support aircraft. The unidentified Pucheng aircraft could represent another, quite different part of that wider effort — or something else altogether. At the same time, this aircraft is roughly 20 percent dimensionally smaller than the MQ-25, which would mean it would have less fuel to give. It’s also worth noting that Boeing’s MQ-25 emerged from an unmanned combat air vehicle (UCAV) design that included low-observable features. Multirole UCAV concepts predating it also looked very similar. The MRE concept from Lockheed during the 1990s looks very similar to the MQ-25 we know today. (Lockheed Martin) In addition, Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), for instance, the FQ-42 Vengeance, and also the XQ-67 Off-Board Sensing Station share a similar overall design. With this in mind, and remembering its different nose section, this could just as easily be a true multirole UCAV or even a CCA, such as one designed for force protection of high-value aerial assets, and it may not even be carrier-capable. Rupprecht cautioned that the manufacturer of the mystery drone remains unidentified. However, one of the more interesting clues about the aircraft’s possible origins comes from Shenyang Aircraft Corporation (SAC). Rupprecht pointed to a propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025, which he believes could fit the development lineage of the larger aircraft now visible at Pucheng. The sub-scale propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025. The background reads (rough translation): “Rollout Ceremony for Final Assembly of Shenyang’s First ‘Surrogate Flight Test’ Pilot-Test Verification Platform UAV.” via Chinese internet A smaller, propeller-driven demonstrator could provide a relatively inexpensive way to investigate aerodynamic characteristics, autonomous flight controls, mission systems, and other technologies before progressing to a much larger aircraft. This piston-powered, propeller-driven aircraft with a broadly similar configuration to the MQ-25 was seen in a video flying, as well. 突然想起中国一家民营无人机公司，做过一款MQ-25活塞桨叶版 https://t.co/Y69dfzpLNS pic.twitter.com/IzU08PC8DK — 飞刀 (@chaoyinsukandao) November 18, 2026 Whether the Pucheng aircraft is related to this SAC demonstrator or if it’s an entirely separate program remains unknown. Beyond the external resemblance, there are no indications that they are linked, and the aircraft could just be a general test surrogate platform. The configuration isn’t totally novel in the advanced UAS world. The aircraft’s appearance is also interesting given the location where it has been spotted. Pucheng Neifu Airport is located in Shaanxi Province, and its surrounding aviation facilities include an area identified in Apple Maps as the National Aeronautics Industrial Base Pucheng General Aviation Industrial Park Guanliban. The industrial park has its own smaller runway, separate from the main airport infrastructure. A close-up of Pucheng with no drones visible, as of June 16, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 The site had remained relatively obscure to outside observers until roughly the past one to two years, according to Rupprecht. More recently, however, various aircraft manufacturers have apparently been conducting testing there. This raises the possibility that Pucheng is not simply an individual manufacturer’s flight-test location, but a facility used by multiple organizations developing and evaluating uncrewed aircraft. Rupprecht also raised the possibility that Pucheng could potentially be a specialized uncrewed aircraft testing facility associated with China’s Flight Test Establishment at Xi’an, commonly known as CFTE. “I cannot say (yet) whether this — and this is my theory — is effectively a branch of the CFTE at Xi’an, which is for crewed and this is a base for uncrewed ones,” Rupprecht explained. A satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor provides an overview of Pucheng as of April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor If Pucheng does serve as a shared testing location for multiple manufacturers, it could help explain the appearance of several otherwise unrelated UAV designs at the same site. Returning to the mystery drone, the combination of its apparent size, configuration, and possible connection to earlier Chinese demonstrator programs makes it an interesting development to watch. Regardless, for now, the imagery from Pucheng offers a glimpse of a potentially significant new Chinese uncrewed aircraft program. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post Mysterious MQ-25 Stingray-Like Chinese Drone Emerges At Little-Known Flight Test Center appeared first on TWZ .

由于人工智能行业的担忧，台湾股市录得创纪录的周跌幅
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月20日电 分析师称，由于对人工智能(AI)行业的担忧，包括美国的出口限制和围绕芯片制造商英伟达公司的不确定性，动摇了投资者的信心，本周台湾股市暴跌17.5%，创历史新高。
台湾证券交易所 (TWSE) 基准指数周五下跌 2,393.60 点，跌幅 6.23%，至 36,033.29 点，为七个月以来的最低水平，也是有记录以来第三大单日跌幅。营业额总计 8,773.5 亿元新台币（266.1 亿美元）。
7 月 17 日下跌 2,953.71 点，周一下跌 2,635.04 点，超过周五跌幅，台交所本周下跌 7,641.83 点，跌幅 17.5%。
资本投资管理公司总经理范振鸿将市场大幅下跌归因于美国中期选举结果、围绕英伟达的不确定性以及美国对中国人工智能芯片出口管制的收紧。
他表示，选举结果突显了美国对人工智能数据中心扩张的反对日益强烈，这可能会减缓未来的建设速度。
范表示，黄仁勋因涉嫌与中国间谍及其下属发生婚外情而辞去英伟达首席执行官职务，再加上该芯片制造商 5300 亿美元的人工智能融资交易的不确定性，继续给市场带来压力。
他补充说，华盛顿对新加坡和其他四个国家的数据中心运营商加强审查的新规定，旨在遏制对中国的非法人工智能芯片出口，加剧了人们对人工智能需求的担忧，给台湾股市带来进一步压力。
尽管金监会在过去11天内推出了两轮遏制卖空的措施，包括禁止做空股票，但台湾股市继续下跌，而前一天跌幅至少为3.5%。
第一创业管理有限公司董事长黄毅庭表示，市场笼罩在恐惧之中，投资者纷纷抛售股票，信心崩溃，很难根据基本面或技术指标来评估市场。
但他仍对恐慌消退后市场反弹持乐观态度，称尽管经济放缓，但对计算能力的强劲需求将维持数据中心建设，而台湾在供应链中的作用将难以替代。

Taiwan stocks suffer record weekly loss amid AI industry concerns
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 20 (CNA) Taiwan stocks plunged a record 17.5 percent this week as concerns over the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, including U.S. export restrictions and uncertainty surrounding chipmaker Nvidia Corp., rattled investor confidence, analysts said.
The Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's (TWSE) benchmark index, fell 2,393.60 points, or 6.23 percent, Friday to 36,033.29, its lowest level in seven months and third-largest one-day point drop on record. Turnover totaled NT$877.35 billion (US$26.61 billion).
Friday's decline was exceeded only by drops of 2,953.71 points on July 17 and 2,635.04 points Monday, leaving the Taiex down 7,641.83 points, or 17.5 percent, for the week.
Fan Chen-hung (范振鴻), general manager of Capital Investment Management Corp., attributed the sharp market decline to U.S. midterm election results, uncertainty surrounding Nvidia and a tightening of U.S. controls on AI chip exports to China.
He said the election results highlighted growing opposition to AI data center expansion in the U.S., which could slow future construction.
Fan said Jensen Huang's (黃仁勳) departure as Nvidia CEO amid allegations of extramarital affairs with a Chinese spy, and a subordinate, coupled with uncertainty over the chipmaker's US$530 billion in AI financing deals, continued to weigh on the market.
He added that Washington's new rules tightening scrutiny of data center operators in Singapore and four other countries to curb illegal AI chip exports to China had fueled concerns over AI demand, putting further pressure on Taiwan stocks.
Taiwan stocks continued to fall despite two rounds of measures introduced by the Financial Supervisory Commission's over the past 11 days to curb short selling, including a ban on shorting stocks that fell at least 3.5 percent the previous day.
First Capital Management Chairman Huang Yi-ting (黃詣庭) said the market was gripped by fear, with investors dumping stocks and confidence collapsing, making it difficult to assess the market based on fundamentals or technical indicators.
But he remained optimistic about a market rebound once panic subsides, saying strong demand for computing power would sustain data center construction despite a slowdown, while Taiwan's role in the supply chain would be difficult to replace.

content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

content:
黄循财总理（左三）星期六（11月21日）在北京钓鱼台国宾馆与中国国务院总理李强（右一）会晤。 （海峡时报）
黄循财总理星期六（11月21日）在北京与中国国务院总理李强举行双边会谈。黄总理指出，新中双边合作联合委员会（JCBC）即将举行新一轮会议，预计将达成超过20项合作成果。
黄总理在北京钓鱼台国宾馆举行的会谈开场时说，中国副总理丁薛祥将来新出席JCBC会议。黄总理说，会议的合作成果将涵盖贸易、数码化、金融一体化、科研创新、医疗和教育等领域，反映新中合作的广度与深度。
黄总理指出，全球环境变得更加不确定和复杂，新加坡和中国因此更有必要加强伙伴关系，共同应对挑战，并开拓新的合作领域，为区域稳定与繁荣作出贡献。
这是黄总理2024年5月上任以来，第四次与李强举行双边会谈。上一次是去年10月李强正式访问新加坡期间。
黄总理在会谈开场时回顾，李强去年10月正式访问新加坡时，两人就如何进一步深化双边关系展开富有建设性的讨论。此后，两国持续推进全方位高质量的前瞻性伙伴关系。
他也指出，新中在苏州、天津和重庆的三个政府间合作项目也持续取得良好进展。这些项目显示两国伙伴关系如何与时俱进，在互信基础上为双方带来实际利益。
李强在开场时则说，当前国际经济局势充满不确定性，“理性国家更应当紧密地协作，携手促进开放发展，为本地区乃至全球稳定繁荣，注入更多的正能量”。
李强指出，近年来在双方共同努力下，新中关系保持良好发展势头，互利合作取得丰硕成果。他说，中国国家主席习近平星期五（20日）与黄总理会晤，也为进一步深化两国关系作出战略指引。
“中新作为传统的友好邻邦，中方愿意同新方加强战略沟通，拓展务实合作，推动两国全方位高质量前瞻性伙伴关系能够取得更多的务实成果，持续增进两国民众的福祉。”
两人会晤后将共进午餐。黄总理随后将结束为期四天的中国工作访问，于下午启程返回新加坡。
这是黄总理上任以来第三次访华。他此行先到深圳出席亚太经济合作组织（APEC）峰会，再前往北京，其间也会见了习近平和北京市委书记尹力。

title: Jensen Huang question gets reporter ejected from Trump-Xi-Putin summit
zh_title: 黄仁勋提问导致记者被驱逐出特朗普-习近平-普京峰会
summary: 据报道，一名彭博社记者在中国共产党领导人在场的情况下向美国总统提出敏感问题后，被逐出美国、中国和俄罗斯领导人之间的历史性三边会议。据《华盛顿邮报》报道，彭博新闻社首席政治记者、该媒体主要节目《彭博监控》联合主持人安娜玛丽·霍登问道：“特朗普总统，黄仁勋是否对美国不忠？”随后，第二位记者开始在 Ch 之前问第二个问题。
content:
据报道，一名彭博社记者在中国共产党领导人在场的情况下向美国总统提出敏感问题后，被逐出美国、中国和俄罗斯领导人之间的历史性三边会议。据《华盛顿邮报》报道，彭博新闻社首席政治记者、该媒体主要节目《彭博监控》联合主持人安娜玛丽·霍登问道：“特朗普总统，黄仁勋是否对美国不忠？”随后，第二名记者开始提出第二个问题，随后中国官员让该小组闭嘴。目前尚不清楚特朗普是否能够回答这两个问题。福克斯新闻的白宫高级记者雅基·海因里希（Jacqui Heinrich）10日表示，亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会的东道国中国告诉记者，“大声提问被认为是极其粗鲁的”，任何这样做的人“都会被从房间里拉出来”，这可能暗示了这一决定的背后是提问的性质，而不是其内容。黄仁勋突然辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，成为过去几周的重大丑闻。
尽管他承认有外遇，但他没有透露第三方的名字，据报道是 Megaspeed 的中国高管 Alice Huang，她还被指控将价值 75 亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国，并向中国情报部门传递信息。 近年来，美国和中国一直陷入竞争，人工智能是中国共产党重点发展的行业之一。这场争夺人工智能“霸主地位”的竞赛导致白宫对其最强大的芯片实施出口管制，并禁止包含美国技术的硬件进入中国。但即使特朗普来了个180度大转弯，最终在2025年12月允许英伟达H100芯片进入中国，只要该公司能够获得出口许可证，英伟达最先进的Blackwell和即将推出的Vera Rubin芯片对中国企业来说仍然遥不可及。除此之外，华盛顿还正在堵住一个漏洞，该漏洞允许中国人工智能公司通过将数据导出到位于其他国家的数据中心来利用美国的计算能力。尽管有这些控制措施，人工智能芯片走私的谣言仍然存在，包括 Supermicro 联合​​创始人 Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw 在内的一些人因芯片转移而被捕。中国还对其记者实施更严格的控制并审查敏感话题。作为APEC峰会和三边会议的东道主，它可以排除它认为违反其标准的记者。
海因里希表示，白宫主张霍登参加三边会议，但中方似乎拒绝对他们的决定做出让步。

【原文 English Original】
A Bloomberg reporter was ejected from a historic trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China, and Russia after reportedly asking a sensitive question to the U.S. President while in the presence of the leader of the Chinese Communist Party. According to The Washington Post , Bloomberg News journalist Annmarie Hordern, the chief political correspondent and co-host of the media outlet’s leading program, Bloomberg Surveillance , asked, “President Trump, has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?” A second reporter had then started asking a second question before Chinese officials shushed the group. It’s unclear if Trump was able to answer both these questions. Senior White House Correspondent for Fox News Jacqui Heinrich said on X that China, the host country of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit where the trilateral meeting was happening along the side, told journalists that “yelling questions is considered extremely rude” and that anyone doing so “will be pulled from the room,” possibly implying the nature of the questions' delivery, rather than its content, was behind the decision. Jensen Huang’s sudden resignation as the CEO of Nvidia has been a major scandal in the past few weeks. Even though he admitted to having an affair, he did not name the third party, reported to be Alice Huang, a Chinese executive for Megaspeed who’s also accused of diverting $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips into China and passing along information to Chinese intelligence. The U.S. and China have been locked in a rivalry in recent years, with artificial intelligence being one of the industries that the Chinese Communist Party is focusing on. This race to achieve “supremacy” in AI has led the White House to impose export controls on its most powerful chips and to bar hardware containing U.S. tech from making its way into China. But even though Trump made a 180-degree turn and finally allowed Nvidia H100 chips into China in December 2025, provided the company can secure export licenses, the most advanced Blackwell and upcoming Vera Rubin chips from Nvidia are still out of reach for Chinese companies. Aside from that, Washington is also closing a loophole that allowed Chinese AI firms to take advantage of American compute by exporting their data to data centers located in other countries. Despite all those controls, rumors of AI chip smuggling still persist, with several individuals, including Supermicro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw , getting arrested for chip diversion. China also puts tighter control on its journalists and censors sensitive topics. As the host of the APEC summit and the trilateral meeting, it could exclude reporters that it thinks violate its standards. Heinrich said that the White House advocated for Hordern’s inclusion in the trilateral meeting, but it seems that the Chinese refused to budge on their decision.

content:
韩联社首尔11月20日电 韩国统一部长官郑东泳20日上午在中央政府首尔办公大楼会见美国驻韩国大使米歇尔·斯蒂尔，双方就韩半岛局势和对朝政策交换意见。
11月20日，在中央政府首尔办公大楼，郑东泳（右）会见斯蒂尔。 韩联社
郑东泳祝贺斯蒂尔履任美国驻韩大使并表示，期待斯蒂尔大使推动韩美关系进一步巩固和发展。他强调，对于实现韩半岛和平稳定，韩美合作必不可少，韩美两国应该基于坚固的韩美同盟，重启韩朝及朝美对话，实现韩半岛永久和平。他还介绍了韩国政府为防范韩朝非军事区（DMZ）发生偶发性军事冲突、构建韩半岛永久和平机制所付出的努力，并呼吁美方继续给予支持与配合。
这是斯蒂尔自今年7月底来韩履新以来时隔四个月首次与郑东泳会面。美国驻韩大使通常在履新1个月之内拜会韩国统一部长官。从以往惯例来看，斯蒂尔此次拜会郑东泳的时间明显晚于惯例。而且，斯蒂尔已经会见过外交部长官赵显、产业通商部长官金正官、国防部长官姜信哲等主要部门首长。分析认为，郑东泳此前发表“朝鲜龟城铀浓缩设施”相关言论，导致美方决定不与韩方共享部分涉朝信息，斯蒂尔迟迟未拜会郑东泳背后可能有与此相关的考量。
郑东泳当天下午将在板门店会见联合国军司令兼驻韩美军司令泽维尔·布伦森。统一部长官与联合国军司令会面实属罕见，上一次还是2023年11月时任统一部长官金暎浩访问位于平泽市的联合国军司令部，并与联合国军司令会面。
据介绍，郑东泳为考察“自由之家”并慰问工作人员而安排板门店访问行程，联合国军司方面则提议布伦森陪同考察。自由之家由统一部管辖，是位于板门店韩方一侧最前沿的建筑。（完）

印度海军已表示有兴趣支持开发旋转爆震发动机（RDE）驱动的超音速海军导弹。该问题陈述是在 2026 年 10 月举行的 Swavlamban 2026 海军旗舰展览期间发布的纲要的一部分，旨在展示国防创新。问题陈述的全文如下：该问题陈述确定了与旋转爆震发动机 (RDE) 研究相关的拟议本土超音速海军导弹计划。 RDE 研究将旋转爆炸作为推进原理。面临的挑战是确定它是否为所述海军应用提供可靠、可支持的能力途径。评估应区分科学可行性、组件成熟度、综合演示准备情况和服务使用资格。需要独立的证据来证实所声称的相对于现有推进替代方案的优势。该计划应在整个评估过程中保持明确的要求、配置控制、专家安全监督和结果的可追溯性。国内设计所有权、制造可重复性、环境适应性和长期支持是核心考虑因素。预期结果是对可行性和成熟度进行基于证据的评估，并得到授权研究和评估的支持。
在其他航空航天应用中取得的进展不应被视为海军导弹已做好准备的证明。燃气轮机和冲压发动机等传统发动机通过亚音速燃烧过程（也称为爆燃）产生推力。爆震发动机利用持续超音速燃烧（也称为爆震）产生的冲击波来产生推力。这意味着，对于相似的尺寸和重量等级，与燃气轮机或冲压发动机相比，爆震发动机不仅可以提供更大的推力，而且可以提供更高的效率。一家名为 D-Propulse Aerospace 的印度初创公司于 2026 年 7 月在 DRDO 测试设施测试了 RDE 原型机，在 24 小时内进行了五次静态测试。 D-Propulse 随后公布了开发 RDE 动力的吸气式超音速巡航导弹和旋转爆震火箭发动机 (RDRE) 动力的微型 SAM 的计划，用于反 UAS 应用。 《海军新闻》联系了创始人兼首席执行官 Saurav Jha，询问该公司对海军问题陈述的看法：D-Propulse 打算利用其吸气式 RDE 技术来制造超音速巡航导弹，这种导弹比传统系统更小、更便宜，但仍能达到作战射程。这将允许迄今为止只能承载距离更短的系统的平台进行承载。较低的价格将使印度军方能够实现真正的大规模精确化。
毕竟，超音速巡航导弹比其他类型的系统到达目标的概率要高得多。因此，超音速巡航导弹的弹匣深度是当今情况下的关键要求，我们的目标价格点应该能够实现这一点。 D-Propulse 的马赫 3 超音速巡航导弹的 CAD 渲染图（图片来自 D-Propulse） 在回答有关与海军就 RDE 海军导弹进行谈判的问题时，Jha 表示，D-Propulse 一直在与相关利益相关者就其正在开发的系统进行磋商，包括通过既定机制寻求支持。在海德拉巴测试的发动机已在 Swavlamban 2026 上展出，是经过验证的发动机

【原文 English Original】
The Indian Navy has expressed interest in supporting the development of a Rotating Detonation Engine (RDE) – powered supersonic naval missile. The problem statement was part of a compendium released during Swavlamban 2026, the Navy’s flagship exhibition meant to showcase defence innovation, held in October 2026. The full text of the problem statement is as follows: This problem statement identifies a proposed indigenous supersonic naval missile programme associated with Rotating Detonation Engine (RDE) research. RDE research examines rotating detonation as a propulsion principle. The challenge is to establish whether it offers a credible, supportable capability pathway for the stated naval application. The assessment should distinguish scientific feasibility, component maturity, integrated demonstrator readiness and qualification for service use. Independent evidence is required to substantiate claimed advantages against established propulsion alternatives. The programme should maintain clear requirements, configuration control, specialist safety oversight and traceability of results throughout its evaluation. Domestic design ownership, manufacturing repeatability, environmental suitability and long-term support are central considerations. The expected outcome is an evidence-based assessment of feasibility and maturity, supported by authorised research and evaluation. Demonstrated progress in another aerospace application should not be treated as proof of readiness for a naval missile. Traditional engines like gas turbines and ramjets generate thrust by subsonic combustion process, also known as deflagration. Detonation engines utilize the shockwaves generated due to sustained supersonic combustion, also known as detonation, to generate thrust. This means that for a similar size and weight class, detonation engines can not only provide greater thrust but also better efficiency compared to gas turbines or ramjets. An Indian startup named D-Propulse Aerospace had tested an RDE prototype at a DRDO test facility in July 2026, conducting five static tests in 24 hours. D-Propulse subsequently unveiled plans to develop RDE powered air-breathing supersonic cruise missiles and rotating detonation rocket engine (RDRE) powered micro-SAMs for counter-UAS applications. Naval News reached out to founder and CEO Saurav Jha to inquire about the firm’s views regarding the Navy’s problem statement: D-Propulse intends to leverage its air-breathing RDE technology to build supersonic cruise missiles that are much smaller and cheaper than legacy systems and yet reach operational ranges. This would allow carriage by platforms that hitherto could only carry much shorter ranged systems. The lower price point will enable true mass in precision for the Indian military. After all, supersonic cruise missiles have a much higher probability of arrival over target than other types of systems out there. So, having magazine depth for supersonic cruise missiles is a key requirement in today’s scenario and our target price point should enable that. CAD Rendering of D-Propulse’s Mach 3 Supersonic Cruise Missile (Image via D-Propulse) In response to a question regarding talks with the Navy for the RDE naval missile, Jha stated that D-Propulse has been in consultation with the relevant stakeholders for the system it is developing, including for support through established mechanisms. The engine tested at Hyderabad was put on display at Swavlamban 2026 and is the proof motor of a flight-capable design. Naval News has learnt that based on that test data, new iterations will be fabricated and tested at the company’s newly constructed large connected-pipe Combustor Test Facility. D-Propulse aims to compress the developmental cycle significantly with this facility and has offered the facility to other small engine developers. Naval News also requested comments from Jha regarding the rationale behind the planned development of the RDRE micro-SAM: The idea behind the RDRE-powered micro SAM is to flip the economics of war in the favour of the defender. RDRE-powered micro-SAMs will be faster and more maneuverable than existing systems, allowing the user to address a wider range of incoming subsonic loitering munitions. Our studies show that RDRE technology can bring down the cost of effective systems greatly, perhaps even to the point of these being seen as ‘consumable ammunition’ if the production runs are large enough. And given the saturation scenarios we are seeing across conflict zones such as the Persian Gulf, where literally thousands of low-RCS subsonic munitions are being lobbed at air defence networks, I believe that our RDRE power counter UAS micro SAM will be required in very significant numbers in the near future. D-Propulse intends to offer the air-breathing RDE powered supersonic cruise missile for user trials by the end of 2029 and intends to offer the RDRE powered micro-SAM by mid-2028. Globally, extensive work is being done in the United States on developing RDE technology. Under the DARPA GAMBIT program, RTX’s Pratt & Whitney had completed a series of RDE tests in 2025. AFRL has also worked on RDE technology and recently expressed interest in combined-cycle RDRE , seeking a flight demonstration to validate the system’s operational viability. GE Aerospace had tested turbine- based combined-cycle RDE in 2023. In January 2026, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace demonstrated a liquid fuel RDE for missiles. Venus Aerospace , L3Harris and IN Space LLC are also developing various types of detonation engines. In the Indian context, an RDE powered supersonic missile would be complementary to the BrahMos . While the latter with its proven production run and ever increasing range will remain the mainstay weapon of the Navy, lighter subsonic and supersonic missiles are likely to proliferate due to cost and weight benefits. Missiles like the NASM-SR and NASM-MR are being developed by DRDO. The lighter form factor of an RDE powered naval missile may make it analogous to the BrahMos NG, which is currently in the R&D stage. Dr. Jaiteerth Joshi, CEO of BrahMos Aerospace, recently told ANI that the first model of BrahMos NG is expected by 2029. Once fabricated, several rounds of trials are required before the missile can be inducted. Dr. Joshi also confirmed the development of a 1,500 km ranged version of the BrahMos, up from the current maximum of about 800 km . The range extension will continue to occur in a phased manner and the 1,500 km range version has been designed and is currently undergoing simulations. BrahMos Aerospace has a nearly a full orderbook and continues to bag export orders. After ordering three batteries for $370 million in 2022 , the Philip p ines is reportedly exploring purchase of “at least six additional BrahMos batteries.” India has also offered to explore the integration of BrahMos on Philippine naval vessels. Five Akash SAM regiments and the Pinaka MLRS are also being looked at by the Philippine Marines and Army, Firstpost reported. Earlier, India’s defence secretary had confirmed that initial deals were signed with two more countries in Southeast Asia for the BrahMos. Vietnam is likely to receive a single coastal battery worth about $100 million while Indonesia has signed two $100 million contracts. Both countries are expected to place larger orders in the coming years. Philippine Marines showcase the BrahMos anti-ship missile system for the first time during the service’s 75th anniversary. More on Swavlamban 2026 Other notable firms with flagship projects present at Swavlamban 2026 included: Sagar Defence Engineering which developed the Matangi USV. Sagar Defence has commenced delivery of 12 meter class USVs to the Navy in 2026 after receiving an order for 12 USVs. Xinfinti Aerospace is developing Naval Chetak Autonomous System (NCAS). NCAS is supported by the Navy under iDEX program and seeks to convert HAL Chetak helicopters into uncrewed assets, an endeavor attempted and aborted by a HAL – IAI combine in the 2010s. Kalam Labs has obtained an iDEX contract from the Navy for the development of floating aircraft carriers. Co-founder Ahmed Faraaz told Naval News that the product will be an airship that can transport Kalam Labs’ suite of propeller driven high-altitude proven swarm-capable UAVs to altitudes exceeding 50,0000 feet. The altitude will enable the airship to stay protected from anti-aircraft munitions while conducting ISR and deploying UAVs for various tasks. Kalam Labs has deployed its UAVs from altitudes greater than 100,000 feet using balloons. Faraaz told Naval News that the firm has also bagged iDEX contracts from IAF for development of a supersonic autonomous spaceplane and mesh enabled space drone swarms. The post Indian Navy Exploring Development of Rotating Detonation Engine Powered Supersonic Cruise Missile appeared first on Naval News .

國民黨台北市長候選人蔣萬安（左起）、民進黨台北市長候選人沈伯洋日前在電視辯論會上合影，各自以手勢比出號次。（中央社檔案照片）
（中央社記者葉蓁芸、劉建邦台北20日電）第二場台北市長選舉公辦政見發表會明天下午2時舉行，台北市長蔣萬安將聚焦台北願景；民進黨市長候選人沈伯洋則將講述公務員減壓等政見。
根據北市選委會資料，市長選舉公辦政見發表會共2場，分別於14日、21日下午辦理，2人一組，當天抽籤決定發言順序，每人發言時間30分鐘。
北市選委會表示，21日下午2時5分至下午3時6分由3號沈伯洋、6號唐新民發言；下午3時10分至下午4時11分由4號蕭文乾、5號蔣萬安發言；下午4時15分至下午5時16分則是1號郭璽、2號林志成發言時間。
蔣萬安日前表示，第二場政見會聚焦台北願景，從城市角度向市民報告；沈伯洋則在第一次政見發表會時表示，第二場將講述公務員減壓等政見。
北市選委會指出，依公職人員選舉罷免法、公職人員選舉公辦政見發表會實施辦法規定，並審酌各參選人參加公辦政見發表會意願，市長、議員選舉均採用一輪式辦理公辦政見發表會，透過有線電視系統公用頻道（第3頻道）及YouTube影音平台直播。（編輯：張銘坤）1151120

content:
经过一周繁忙的发射活动，本周全球发射清单预计将进行六次发射，其中包括范登堡发射的 3 次 SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号发射任务、中国的两次发射任务以及南美洲的阿丽亚娜 6 号发射任务。 SpaceX 将为美国太空部队和国家侦察办公室发射有效载荷，而本周的中国任务和阿丽亚娜 6 号任务中至少有一次将发射一批互联网卫星。长征2D |有效载荷未知，将于 11 月 18 日星期三从中国发射，长征 2D (CZ-2D) 预计将于世界标准时间 22:50 从太原卫星发射中心的 9 号发射场 (LC-9) 发射。官方警告通知表明发射轨迹是向南的，但有效载荷及其预定轨道的详细信息要等到发射后才会发布。两级、40.77 米高的 CZ-2D 由上海航天技术研究院 (SAST) 制造。 2D 版本不需要额外的捆绑式助推器。此次飞行将是长征2D的第108次飞行，也是今年的第七次。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX 将于 11 月 18 日星期三进行本周两次发射中的第一次发射，发射时间为四小时，发射窗口于太平洋标准时间晚上 7:00（世界标准时间周四 03:00）开始。
USSF-317 任务是美国太空军 (USSF) 本周的唯一任务，将从加利福尼亚州范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 的东 4 号航天发射场 (SLC-4E) 发射，向东南飞行，将其机密有效载荷送入低地球轨道 (LEO)。所有系统看起来都很好，天气也有利于升空。猎鹰 9 号发射的 USSF-627 任务即将开始从加利福尼亚州发射推进剂 → https://t.co/IdlZbviZZl pic.twitter.com/fKxyN4DIui — SpaceX (@SpaceX) 2026 年 11 月 12 日助推器 B1100 将支持此次任务，这是自近一年前 11 月 23 日首次支持星链集团 11-30 以来的第十一次飞行， 2025 年。除了 NROL-105 和 USSF-385 之外，助推器之前的八次飞行支持了星链任务。 SpaceX 的西海岸无人机飞船 Of Course I Still Love You 将在 B1100 升空后约 8 分钟着陆时驻扎在地面。猎鹰 9 号是一枚直径 3.9 米、高 70 米的两级火箭。九台 Merlin 1D 发动机为第一级助推器提供动力，而第二级则使用一台真空优化的 Merlin 发动机。猎鹰 9 号和猎鹰重型火箭是第一批实现定期重复使用的轨道火箭，其中一枚猎鹰助推器已飞行 37 次。飞行后，两个有效载荷整流罩也被回收并重复使用。长征8A | SatNet LEO Group 本周的第二次中国发射计划于 11 月 11 日星期五举行。
世界标准时间 20 日 11:00，在中国文昌航天发射场的商业 LC-1 发射台上发射。长征 8A (CZ-8A) 将携带 9 颗通信卫星进入近地轨道，这些卫星由 SatNet 拥有并由中国卫星网络集团运营。 CZ-8A火箭有两个直径3.35米的级，总高度为50.54 m。第一级由两个捆绑式液体燃料助推器辅助。此次飞行将标志着 CZ-8A 的第 13 次飞行，也是 2026 年的第七次飞行。 NROL-136 SpaceX 本周的第二次猎鹰 9 号任务定于 11 月 21 日星期六太平洋标准时间凌晨 4:30（世界标准时间 12:30）发射，同样是从加州 VSFB 的 SLC-4E 发射。 NROL-136 任务将携带未知数量的有效载荷进入近地轨道，供国家侦察办公室 (NRO) 的增殖建筑星座使用，该星座由 Space 建造

【原文 English Original】
Following a week of busy launch activity, the worldwide launch manifest is set to see six launches this week, with three SpaceX Falcon 9 missions from Vandenberg, two Chinese missions, and an Ariane 6 mission from South America. SpaceX will launch payloads for the United States Space Force and the National Reconnaissance Office, while at least one of this week’s Chinese missions and the Ariane 6 will launch a batch of internet satellites. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload Wednesday, Nov. 18, will see a launch from China, with a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) expected to launch from Launch Complex 9 (LC-9) at the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center at 22:50 UTC. Official warning notices indicate a southerly launch trajectory, but details of the payload and its intended orbit will not be released until after launch. The two-stage, 40.77-m-tall CZ-2D is manufactured by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST). The 2D variant requires no additional strap-on boosters. This flight will mark the 108th CZ-2D to fly, the seventh of this year. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX’s first of two launches this week comes on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at the start of a four-hour launch window that opens at 7:00 PM PST (03:00 UTC on Thursday). The only mission for the United States Space Force (USSF) this week, the USSF-317 mission will launch from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) in California, flying southeast to place its classified payload into low-Earth orbit (LEO). All systems are looking good, and weather is favorable for liftoff. Propellant load is about to begin for Falcon 9’s launch of the USSF-627 mission from California → https://t.co/IdlZbviZZl pic.twitter.com/fKxyN4DIui — SpaceX (@SpaceX) November 12, 2026 Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its eleventh flight since first supporting Starlink Group 11-30 nearly a year ago on Nov. 23, 2025. Eight of the booster’s previous flights supported Starlink missions, in addition to flying NROL-105 and USSF-385. SpaceX’s west coast droneship, Of Course I Still Love You, will be stationed downrange for B1100’s landing approximately eight minutes after liftoff. Falcon 9 is a 3.9-m-diameter, 70-m-tall two-stage rocket. Nine Merlin 1D engines power the first-stage booster, while the second stage uses a single vacuum-optimized Merlin engine. Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy were the first orbital rockets to achieve regular re-use, with one Falcon booster having flown 37 flights. The two payload fairings are also recovered and reused after flight. Chang Zheng 8A | SatNet LEO Group The second Chinese launch of the week is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, at 11:00 UTC from the Commercial LC-1 pad at the Wenchang Space Launch Site in China. A Chang Zheng 8A (CZ-8A) will carry nine communications satellites into LEO, with the satellites owned by SatNet and operated by the China Satellite Network Group. The CZ-8A rocket features two 3.35-m-diameter stages, with a total height of 50.54 m. The first stage is assisted by two strap-on liquid-fuelled boosters. This flight will mark the 13th overall CZ-8A flight, the seventh of 2026. Falcon 9 | NROL-136 SpaceX’s second Falcon 9 mission of the week is scheduled to launch on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 4:30 AM PST (12:30 UTC), again from SLC-4E at VSFB in California. The NROL-136 mission will carry an unknown number of payloads into LEO for the National Reconnaissance Office’s (NRO) Proliferated Architecture constellation, built by SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The booster supporting this mission will be B1097, flying for the 14th time. This booster first flew on Sept. 3, 2025, and has previously flown eight Starlink missions, as well as NROL-172, Transporter 17, Sentinel-6B, Twilight (Pandora & Others), and USSF-259. Following stage separation, B1097 will conduct a return-to-launch-site landing at Landing Zone 4 (LZ-4), located directly next to SLC-4E. Ariane 64 | Amazon Leo (LE-04) Amazon is continuing to put together its constellation of Leo satellites and will add another 36 on Monday, Nov. 23, at 10:12 UTC aboard an Ariane 64. The rocket will launch from Ensemble de Lancement Ariane 4 (ELA-4) at the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana, with the launch window lasting five hours and 27 minutes. Ariane 64 will follow a northeastern trajectory, delivering 22,000 kg of Leo satellites into LEO. Ariane 64 is a 62-m-tall, 5.4-m-diameter, expendable two-stage rocket built by the ArianeGroup on behalf of the European Space Agency. Both stages are powered by liquid hydrogen and oxygen-fuelled engines. The 64 variant of the basic Ariane 6 utilizes four P129 strap-on solid rocket boosters to provide additional lift-off thrust.
